title: Orientation Estimation of Cryo-EM Images for Molecules with Arbitrary Symmetry by Semidefinite Programming
abstract: This paper extends the non-unique games framework introduced in Bandeira et al. (2020) to address symmetric structures. Precisely, we consider the problem \[ \begin{aligned} \underset{g_1,\ldots,g_n\in \mathcal{G}}{\operatorname{min}}\,\, \frac{1}{|S|}\sum_{i,j=1}^n \sum_{s\in S} f_{ij}(g_i s g_j^{-1}), \end{aligned} \] where $\mathcal{G}$ is a compact group, $S\subset \mathcal{G}$ is a finite subgroup of symmetry elements, and $f_{ij}:\mathcal{G}\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ is a loss function. A notable example is common lines based orientation estimation of cryo-EM images for molecules with point group symmetry $S$, where $\mathcal{G}$ is the rotation group $\operatorname{SO}(3)$. With a semidefinite programming relaxation, we turn the problem into a convex program that is solved with the alternating direction method of multipliers. Unlike existing approaches which are tailored to specific symmetry groups, ours provides a unified computational framework for addressing all point group symmetries. We demonstrate the applicability of the proposed algorithm on the cryo-EM orientation estimation problem on both simulated and experimental datasets. In particular, our algorithm is effective in generating high-quality ab initio models from only a few class averages computed from experimental images.

title: Physics-Aware Deepfake Detection via Distance-Speech Consistency
abstract: Recent progress in generative models has made talking-head deepfakes highly realistic and easy to create, jeopardizing public trust. However, most audio-visual deepfake detectors rely on lip-speech synchronization and are designed for static, frontal videos, limiting their reliability in dynamic, in-the-wild recordings where the speaker moves and lip cues are degraded or missing. As an alternative, we propose a physics-aware detector for dynamic speaking videos that leverages an acoustic constraint: in real recordings, speech energy varies predictably with speaker-to-camera distance, whereas deepfake generation can break this coupling. Our method combines distance estimates from video with distance-dependent acoustic measures from speech to detect deepfakes. Experiments on in-the-wild benchmarks show that the proposed physical cue is effective in dynamic scenarios, and that it complements lip-sync-based detectors, with a simple ensemble achieving consistent gains across datasets. Codes are available at https://byulharang.github.io/PADD/.

title: dMRI-F: A Foundation Model for Generalizable Diffusion MRI Analysis from Sparse Acquisitions
abstract: Diffusion MRI (dMRI) probes water diffusion within the brain, providing unique information about tissue microstructure and white matter connectivity. High-quality dMRI enables advanced and accurate analyses but demands dense acquisitions, resulting in long scan times and hardware constraints that are often infeasible. Further, dMRI requires dedicated computational methods to support diverse analysis tasks (e.g., parcellation, registration, and synthesis) for both neuroscientific and clinical applications. Here, we present dMRI-F, a foundation model that unifies dMRI data enhancement and downstream tasks across diverse acquisitions and populations, while requiring only minimal acquisition input. dMRI-F is pre-trained with a q-space masked reconstruction task: predicting densely sampled multi-shell data from only six volumes. It learns generalizable latent feature representations of dMRI data, which serve as a core foundation for adapting to diverse downstream tasks, including brain parcellation, brain registration, and cross-modal synthesis. Across nine independently acquired datasets, we demonstrate that dMRI-F outperforms state-of-the-art methods with robust generalization across acquisitions, populations, and tasks. Our results demonstrate dMRI-F's versatility as a general-purpose framework that enables diverse dMRI applications from low-cost, sparse acquisitions.

title: Jumbled Simon's Equivalence and Embeddings
abstract: \emph{Jumbled scattered factors} are a generalisation of scattered factors (or subsequences) where a jumbled scattered factor is obtained from another word by deleting and rearranging letters. For limiting the number of rearrangements, we distinguish $\ell$-jumbled scattered factors where $\ell$ limits the number of letters that may occur rearranged. For instance, $\mathtt{car}$, $\mathtt{start}$, $\mathtt{rat}, \mathtt{cat}$ are jumbled scattered factors of $\mathtt{abstract}$ even though $\mathtt{car}$, $\mathtt{start}$ and $\mathtt{cat}$ are no scattered factors and each need one jumble. An example for a jumbled scattered factor with $2$ jumbles is $\mathtt{tatar}$. In this work, we investigate two problems on jumbled scattered factors from an algorithmic perspective. First, we give algorithms for testing jumbled Simon's equivalence where two words are equivalent if they share the same $\ell$-jumbled scattered factors up to length $k$. Second, we investigate how to count the possible occurrences of a jumbled scattered factor -- the jumbled binomial coefficient. After defining the jumbled binomial coefficient, we study jumbled embeddings and factorisations of such as well.

title: Structured SDEs for Realized GARCH: Continuous-Time Volatility Modelling and Component-Level Analysis
abstract: We propose a structured continuous-time stochastic volatility model for one-day-ahead integrated-variance forecasting. The model introduces a jointly evolving realized-measure state that feeds directly into latent variance dynamics, while correlated Brownian innovations capture return-linked dependence. Parameters are estimated through simulation-based predictive learning, and Monte Carlo simulation forecasts integrated variance. Across 17 equity indices, the proposed model shows strong out-of-sample performance relative to GARCH, GARCH-Itô, Realized GARCH, HAR, and HEAVY benchmarks under QLIKE, MSE, and MAE. Ablation results show that realized-measure feedback provides substantial incremental forecasting value within the proposed framework, while return-linked Brownian dependence contributes more modest complementary gains. The results support incorporating measurement-driven information directly into continuous-time latent volatility dynamics to improve integrated-variance forecasting.

title: From Syndromes to Computation: A General Framework for Logical Operations in Quantum Error-Correcting Codes
abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires error-correcting codes that not only protect quantum information but also support useful logical operations with practical physical realizations. Here we develop a general framework in which the stabilizer syndromes of commuting Pauli rotations directly organize logical-gate design. We derive an exact codespace-preservation condition valid at arbitrary rotation angles, providing a common stabilizer-level description for CSS and non-CSS codes and for both Clifford and non-Clifford operations. A particularly useful equal-syndrome specialization reduces Clifford gate design to stabilizer factorization, yields a general generator weight bound of $\lceil d/2\rceil$ for distance-$d$ codes, and systematically extends to logical rotations higher in the Clifford hierarchy. Applied to bivariate-bicycle (BB) and non-CSS Mirror qLDPC codes, the framework gives explicit low-weight Clifford and controlled-phase gates. Our implementations yield new low-weight gates, including an addressed $T$ gate on the $[[16,4,4]]$ BB code, $T$-type rotations on the $[[64,8,8]]$ BB code, and CCZ-, CS-, and $T$-type operations on the $[[36,6,6]]$ Mirror code. We also develop analytic constructions using Clifford algebra bases, which turn the syndrome constraints into explicit algebraic relations and provide a systematic route to logical addressability. We use this approach to analytically construct addressed CNOT, SWAP, controlled, and CCZ-type gates on recursive hypercube codes. An independent construction on middle quantum Reed--Muller codes yields C${}^r$Z gates that saturate the equal-syndrome weight bound. These results establish stabilizer syndromes as a constructive link between the stabilizer structure of a quantum code, the logical computations it can directly support, and the fault-tolerance properties of their physical realizations.

title: The impact of architecture and cost function on dissipative quantum neural networks
abstract: Abstract Combining machine learning and quantum computation is a potential path towards powerful applications on quantum devices. Among such approaches, quantum neural networks have emerged as a promising framework. In this work, we present a novel architecture for dissipative quantum neural networks (DQNNs) in which each building block can implement any quantum channel, thus introducing a clear notion of universality suitable for the quantum framework. To this end, we reformulate DQNNs using isometries instead of the conventionally used unitaries, thereby reducing the number of parameters in these models. We furthermore derive a versatile one-to-one parametrization of isometries, facilitating the practical implementation of the proposed structure. Focusing on the impact of different objective functions on the optimization process, we numerically investigate the trainability of extended DQNNs. Our results identify the Hilbert-Schmidt distance as a readily measurable cost function that enables efficient and reliable model optimization. These findings advance both the theoretical understanding and the experimental implementability of quantum neural networks.

title: Evaluation of Local Language Models in a RAG System for Educational Assistance
abstract: Este trabajo presenta el desarrollo colaborativo entre la Facultad de Matemática, Astronomía, Física y Computación (FAMAF) de la Universidad Nacional de Córdoba y la empresa Procer Tecnologías S.A.S. para construir un sistema de Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) de asistencia educativa. El sistema está diseñado para ejecutarse en una computadora local a la que se conecta un dispositivo portátil de asistencia diseñado por la empresa, reemplazando el sistema RAG que tiene actualmente desplegado en la nube. Su objetivo es mejorar el acceso autónomo a contenidos escolares para estudiantes con discapacidad visual, dislexia u otras barreras de aprendizaje. La arquitectura implementada combina almacenamiento vectorial, búsqueda híbrida, proceso de reranking y generación de respuestas con modelos de lenguaje ejecutados localmente vía Ollama. Se evaluaron 10 modelos reducidos utilizando un dataset de 396 pares pregunta respuesta en español, construido a partir de documentos y usuarios reales del servicio en la nube de la empresa. Los resultados muestran que la búsqueda híbrida con reranking mejora consistentemente a la búsqueda vectorial pura en las cinco métricas y en todos los modelos evaluados. Notablemente, los modelos evaluados son de tamaño reducido pudiéndose ejecutar en GPUs de uso hogareño, y aun así obtienen métricas competitivas tomando como referencia las respuestas del sistema que la empresa tiene actualmente.

title: The Responsibility Gap in Explainable AI
abstract: This paper critically examines the persistent responsibility gap in explainable artificial intelligence (XAI), arguing that current approaches fail to adequately bridge it. While XAI is often promoted as a remedy for the opacity of AI systems—the so-called “black box problem”—and as a way to enable human accountability in both high- and low-stakes AI applications, I contend that these hopes are premature. The paper distinguishes between legal and moral responsibility, arguing that regulation alone cannot address the full spectrum of responsibility gaps, especially in everyday, low-stakes scenarios. Then, I argue that XAI needs to tackle two separate but interconnected problems in its attempt to bridge the responsibility gap: an epistemological problem concerning the nature of XAI explanations, and a moral attribution problem regarding the distribution of blame and praise in situations where AI is involved in decision-making. Through detailed discussion of XAI methods and their limitations, I demonstrate that existing techniques often provide only post-hoc, technically focused explanations, which are insufficient for grounding moral responsibility. The paper concludes that without fundamental advances in both the design of explanations and our practices of responsibility attribution, the responsibility gap in AI will remain an unresolved and pressing issue for the field.

title: Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning for Coordinated Emergency Building Sweeps
abstract: We develop a Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MADDPG) framework for coordinating emergency responders during building sweeps. The problem is formulated as a Decentralized Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (Dec-POMDP) that captures building topology, occupant vulnerability, dynamic hazards, and partial observability. In the six-room office baseline, MADDPG reaches a 134-second sweep time after 5,000 episodes, within 6.3% of the 126-second theoretical optimum and outperforming PPO and DQN. Extensions to a two-story school and a U-shaped warehouse achieve 120 seconds with five responders and 105 seconds with four responders, respectively, with diminishing returns beyond these staffing levels. Under communication failure, coverage remains about 98% while sweep time rises 15–20%; reduced staffing triggers workload redistribution, and dynamic hazards cause threatened areas to be prioritized. Occupancy sensing, mesh networks, and environmental sensing are projected to reduce sweep time by 35–50%. Sensitivity analysis confirms robust performance across realistic parameter ranges.

title: SBR-3 Combined-Arms Composite Hot-State Battery — The Guarantees Compose (All 6 Falsifiers Pass)
abstract: Combined-arms composite hot-state battery: every previously tested attack class fired together during active learning. 54 exotic composite forgeries were held; 12 inert legs executed as designed (none degraded a live guarantee); 20/20 hot-state probes were contained; 48/48 lineage forgeries were rejected by the crossing audit. Three instrument defects were disclosed between runs, and SIP-2 observations on composite interactions recorded. The guarantees compose: no cross-class interaction opened a gap that single-class batteries left closed. Operator authorization: Leon GO (chat authorization, 11:55 CT, Oct 13, 2026). Scope honesty: single-run preregistered falsifier battery on synthetic data against a prototype governed self-healing system; no production claim is made or implied. Operator authorization recorded as GO + timestamp per the operator-privacy doctrine. This software is a prototype and is provided for educational and research purposes only. It is not intended for production use, commercial deployment, or safety-critical environments. All systems are experimental and may contain defects on them.

title: Analisis Sentimen Kepuasan Masyarakat terhadap Pelayanan Aplikasi Mobile JKN Menggunakan Algoritma Naïve Bayes
abstract: Program Jaminan Kesehatan Nasional (JKN) yang diselenggarakan oleh BPJS Kesehatan sedang memasuki masa transisi kebijakan Kelas Rawat Inap Standar (KRIS) berdasarkan Peraturan Presiden Nomor 59 Tahun 2024. Perubahan kebijakan tersebut memunculkan beragam tanggapan masyarakat yang tersebar pada ulasan aplikasi Mobile JKN di Google Play Store, namun tanggapan tersebut belum diolah menjadi informasi yang dapat dimanfaatkan sebagai bahan evaluasi layanan. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengklasifikasikan sentimen ulasan pengguna aplikasi Mobile JKN menggunakan algoritma Naïve Bayes serta mengimplementasikan hasil klasifikasi ke dalam sistem informasi berbasis web. Data dikumpulkan melalui teknik web scraping terhadap 4.000 ulasan berbahasa Indonesia pada periode 15 Juli sampai dengan 15 Agustus 2026 dan menghasilkan 2.675 ulasan hasil seleksi. Pelabelan dilakukan menggunakan pendekatan rating pengguna dan kamus sentimen InSet dengan verifikasi manual pada ulasan yang kedua pendekatannya berbeda, sehingga diperoleh 751 ulasan berlabel positif dan negatif. Data diproses melalui cleaning, case folding, tokenizing, stopword removal, dan stemming, kemudian dibobotkan menggunakan TF-IDF. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan model Naïve Bayes memperoleh accuracy 90,07%, precision 90,57%, recall 90,07%, dan F1-score 89,99%, sedangkan 10-fold cross validation memperoleh rata-rata akurasi 90,68% dengan simpangan baku 2,60%. Sebaran sentimen menunjukkan 403 ulasan (53,7%) bersentimen negatif dan 348 ulasan (46,3%) bersentimen positif, dengan keluhan pengguna terpusat pada proses autentikasi, khususnya pengiriman kode OTP dan verifikasi akun. Sistem informasi berbasis web yang dibangun berhasil melewati seluruh 12 skenario pengujian Black Box dan dapat digunakan secara berulang untuk menganalisis ulasan pengguna tanpa harus membacanya satu per satu.

title: Scientific Super Intelligence: From Science Tokens to ScienceRSI
abstract: Scientific reasoning moves beyond natural language. The search for a discovery runs across sequences, structures, fields, omics, images and measurements, while language models reason mainly in text. This Perspective sets out four proposals from the Scinetics team. First, we define science tokens: modality-appropriate units of scientific information, spanning native discrete symbols, typed values, continuous representations and learned, decodable codes. A shared interface for these representations would let one model read, write and reason across modalities, so that a chain of science tokens operates on scientifically meaningful states, not on descriptions of them. Second, we define Scientific Super Intelligence (SSI) as a joint crossover: one frozen model that outperforms vertical specialists, such as the AlphaFold series on protein structure prediction, on their own tasks, and outperforms general large language models of the same size on broad scientific reasoning. Capacity, published training precedents, data inventories and compute place the first test of that crossover at 100–300 billion parameters and 10–30 trillion training tokens. Third, we propose ScienceRSI (Science Recursive Self- Improvement) as the route to that window. Following the AI4AI pattern, each larger generation is trained on data that the smaller generation before it produced: the earlier model generates candidate reasoning, screens it and keeps what passes, and in science that screening can be done by a simulation, a database or an experiment. Training this way reduces the dependence on scarce human-written scientific reasoning data and shortens each iteration. Fourth, we propose science-token economics, which separates metered computation from the value of evidence-labelled, reusable scientific assets.

title: Modular Traffic Shaping for Censorship Evasion
abstract: Internet censorship poses a significant threat to the rights of individuals to access information and communicate without interference. Such censorship typically prohibits accessing only certain online content or platforms. As a result, it has become popular to evade censorship using encrypted connections to proxies located outside the censor's view. However, proxied traffic has been shown to exhibit characteristic packet size and timing patterns, which are observable to the censor despite encryption. Such identifying patterns may be eliminated via traffic shaping, where packet sizes and times are intentionally modified by the sender. We propose that traffic shaping be accomplished in proxy systems using a modular traffic shaper and present an API for such a module. Modularization will allow easier experimentation as well as reuse of shaping policies across different proxy systems. We implement a proof-of-concept traffic-shaping module in the Proteus system and conduct experiments showing that it can express a variety of shaping policies.

title: Service Recovery in Chatbot‐mediated Environments: Trust Dynamics and Customer Loyalty Intentions
abstract: Abstract Prior research has shown that customers’ perceptions of chatbots may be influenced by the situational context in which human–chatbot interactions take place. This research advances understanding of artificial intelligence (AI)‐enabled chatbot‐led service failure recovery (SFR) in the context of customer loyalty. Using a social constructivist philosophical perspective and an inductive approach, 52 in‐depth interviews were conducted to capture individuals’ perceptions of chatbot‐led interactions during a SFR process and how these perceptions impacted their trust in, and commitment to, brands. Utilizing commitment‐trust theory and trust transfer theory, we propose a framework that characterizes the relationships between a chatbot‐led SFR process and customer loyalty intentions. Based on the emergent data, customers’ evaluations of a service recovery journey led by chatbots can be grouped into four main outcomes: continued trust in, and commitment to, chatbot and brand; continued trust in, and commitment to, brand; discontinued trust in, and commitment to, chatbot; and discontinued trust in, and commitment to, chatbot and brand. Our findings extend current understanding of how consumers’ trust and commitment during chatbot‐led interactions during SFR evolve and highlight the dynamic relationship between consumers and the context of interactions. This study has theoretical and practical implications for developing and leveraging customers’ loyalty in AI‐enabled chatbot‐led SFR environments.

title: RingNav: Task-Shaped Circular Memory for Visual Heading
abstract: Tiny robots have limited computation and memory, yet visual navigation systems often maintain more state than a task requires. We ask whether persistent memory can instead be shaped by the task. We present \textbf{RingNav}, a \(10.6\)k--parameter visual heading estimator that constrains its memory to the circular manifold \(S^1\). RingNav learns only the turn between consecutive images, while heading is composed directly on the circle. On the TartanAir Visual SLAM Challenge, RingNav reduces mean absolute turn error by \(27\%\) and accumulated heading error over $4$ sec by \(15\%\) relative to a similarly sized learned-memory model. The structured update also gives exactly zero turn for identical frames and exact cancellation under sequence reversal. Without fine-tuning, RingNav transfers to real-world drone experiments and continues estimating heading under severe visual degradation. RingNav runs at $27.3$Hz on Raspberry Pi Zero 2W and can be deployed on an ultra-low power GAP8 processor at $33.4$Hz.

title: Just Respect the Semantics: Image-Token Compression via Pre-LLM Semantic Variable-Resolution Tokenization and In-LLM Relevance Pruning
abstract: Image-token compression must reduce computation without hurting the semantics. We introduce Varest, guided by semantic fungibility: tokens within a coherent semantic region can be summarized coarsely, while object boundaries and literal text require finer distinctions. Object and text localizers guide variable-resolution merging, preserving spatial coverage and finer detail at boundaries and text. Learned [REL] registers then prune visual tokens after early decoder processing. Training across budgets enables one checkpoint per backbone. Across three backbones and 13 benchmarks, Varest outperforms 15 baselines in mean performance retention at every evaluated budget, retaining 86.10-92.33% of full-token performance with only 5.56% of the original layer-averaged image-token count.

title: BELT : BEhavior-Aligned Low-Rank KV Cache Compression with Learned Top-k Rank Allocation
abstract: Long-context inference makes the key-value (KV) cache a major memory bottleneck for large language models. We propose BELT, a low-rank KV cache compression framework. Its key-side objective targets attention distributions rather than raw keys or pre-softmax logits, yielding a quadratic surrogate with a closed-form low-rank solution. A learned global rank allocator uses differentiable soft selection during training and hard selection at deployment to meet a user-specified component budget. Experiments demonstrate improved model quality under aggressive compression and increased decoding throughput at comparable accuracy. Evaluated across three LLMs and multiple benchmarks, BELT achieves up to 70% low-rank KV cache compression while outperforming the strongest baseline by up to 23.3 points on LongBench, and up to 17.8x overall KV cache reduction when combined with quantization. With Triton-based GPU kernels and a quantized cache, BELT delivers up to 2.7x speedup for the attention module and 3.3x end-to-end decoding throughput.

title: Multi-parameter estimation enhanced by level crossing Hamiltonian structure with Bayesian feedback
abstract: Level crossings, where two quantum energy levels intersect, are ubiquitous in quantum systems and play a central role in controlling quantum dynamics. In this study, we establish a framework that connects these level crossing structures to the ultimate precision limits of quantum metrology. By analyzing a Hamiltonian with the level crossings structure, we identify the conditions under which multiple parameters can be estimated simultaneously with maximal sensitivity near the level crossing point. We then construct a resource efficient sensing protocol based on unitary quench dynamics and Bayesian estimation, enabling high precision, low cost parameter estimation without requiring entanglement or complex control. We present a protocol whose estimation precision saturates the Holevo Cramer Rao bound, the tightest achievable precision bound in multi parameter estimation. Using the two level model and the two spin Ising model as illustrative examples, we demonstrate how the protocol can be applied to a system with level crossing Hamiltonian structure. Our findings reveal that level crossings serve as universal operating points for precision quantum metrology, offering a simple and scalable path toward practical multi parameter sensing across diverse quantum platforms.

title: Understanding Machine Taste: Aesthetic Agreement Across Foundation Models in K-pop
abstract: As foundation models enter creative industries, understanding their aesthetic preferences becomes an important step toward AI-assisted creative decision making. In this work, we investigate how foundation models evaluate creative content and characterize their ``machine taste'' using K-pop songs and music videos as a testbed. We formulate aesthetic evaluation as a pairwise ranking problem and systematically examine pairwise inter-model agreement, group-level consensus, and cross-modal preference alignment. Our results reveal stronger pairwise inter-model agreement and group-level consensus in visual evaluation than in audio evaluation, while preferences across the two modalities remain weakly aligned. We further examine how visual consensus rankings relate to real-world popularity using historical YouTube viewership data, finding positive but varying correlations across artist groups. These findings provide initial insights into machine aesthetic preferences and lay the groundwork for future AI-assisted creative decision making that considers creative content, artist identity, audience preferences, and market dynamics.

title: Enhanced weak-field sensing using detuned squeezing
abstract: Achieving measurement precision beyond the standard quantum limit (SQL) is a fundamental object in quantum metrology. In this manuscript, we propose a streamlined protocol for weak signal sensing in a trapped-ion spin-oscillator system that simultaneously exploits detuned motional squeezing and spin-oscillator entanglement. By combining these two quantum resources, the phase accumulation in this spin system is significantly accelerated, as a result achieving an exponential improvement in the sensitivity over unsqueezed cases. Remarkably, we show that the significant metrological gain provided by our protocol persists in noisy environments, with the sensitivity remaining below the SQL. In particular, our protocol retains a distinct advantage in the short interrogation time regime, thus demonstrating the practical potential in quantum-enhanced sensing.

title: Explanation User Interfaces: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: Artificial Intelligence is one of the major technological advancements of this century, bearing incredible potential for users through AI-powered applications and tools in numerous domains. Being often black-box (i.e., its decision-making process is unintelligible), developers typically resort to eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) techniques to interpret the behavior of AI models to produce systems that are transparent, fair, reliable, and trustworthy. However, presenting explanations to the user is not trivial and is often left as a secondary aspect of the system’s design process, leading to AI systems that are not useful to end-users. This paper presents a Systematic Literature Review on Explanation User Interfaces (XUIs) to gain a deeper understanding of the solutions and design guidelines employed in the academic literature to effectively present explanations to users. To improve the contribution and real-world impact of this survey, we also present a platform to support Human-cEnteRed developMent of Explainable user interfaceS (HERMES) and guide practitioners and scholars in the design and evaluation of XUIs.

title: ESPANLI: An Adversarial NLI Benchmark for Río de la Plata Spanish via Human–Model Competitions
abstract: Los benchmarks de Inferencia en Lenguaje Natural (NLI) como SNLI, MultiNLI y ANLI son hoy herramientas estándar para evaluar modelos de lenguaje, pero su cobertura es mayoritariamente inglesa y sus ejemplos resultan crecientemente resolubles por atajos heurísticos o memorización. La evaluación en español, y en particular en la variante rioplatense, está sub-representada; los conjuntos disponibles suelen ser traducciones que distorsionan la superposición léxica, las condiciones de verdad y el contexto pragmático. Describimos el diseño de ESPANLI, un benchmark adversarial de NLI para el español construido a partir de tesis doctorales alojadas en repositorios públicos de universidades argentinas, con fenómenos rioplatenses anotados por curadores especialistas. Su núcleo es una competencia humano-en-el-bucle en la que generadores con formación específica producen instancias que hacen fallar a modelos de referencia y una comisión de verificación conserva sólo los casos validados por mayoría. Las contribuciones previstas incluyen un corpus adversarial público, una plataforma interactiva de generación y un conjunto de sub-tareas de NLI de nivel experto nativas en castellano.

title: China–Armenia Seismic, Strong-Motion and Geodynamic Network
authors: Institute of Geophysics and Engineering Seismology after A. Nazarov
China Earthquake Administration Institute of geophysics
abstract: Permanent network in Armenia, created and operated jointly by the A. Nazarov Institute of Geophysics and Engineering Seismology (IGES) and the Institute of Geophysics, China Earthquake Administration (IGP-CEA), since December 2024. The network currently comprises nine stations. Five integrated stations collocate a broadband seismometer (120 s), a strong-motion accelerometer, a continuous GNSS receiver for geodynamic observations and a weather sensor; four short-period stations complement them. Sensors are installed on isolated piers in underground vaults. Data are transmitted in real time by satellite (VSAT) and 5G to the data center in Gyumri, which also runs earthquake early warning. Aims: seismicity monitoring, strong-motion recording, crustal deformation and seismic hazard assessment. The network records local, regional (Taurus–Caucasus region) and teleseismic earthquakes.

title: Deep-learning for improving prognostication and therapy prediction in breast cancer
abstract: Treatment decisions in early breast cancer depend on accurate prognostication and on therapy-relevant biomarkers, both of which rely largely on examination of routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained tissue. Manual assessment, however, is subject to observer variability and cannot exhaustively quantify tissue features or detect complex morphological associations. Advances in artificial intelligence have therefore prompted the development of computational tools that extract additional information from routine sections. This thesis investigates whether deep learning applied to H&E whole-slide images (WSIs) can improve prognostication beyond established clinicopathological factors and enable inference of therapy-relevant biomarkers in breast cancer. Four studies are presented, addressing (i) the design of a general modeling framework, (ii) the interchangeability of models for assessing an immune biomarker (i.e., tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes), (iii) the inference of molecular alteration from morphology, and (iv) the direct modeling of patient survival. In the first study, we developed a model-agnostic, multiresolution multiple-instance learning (MIL) framework for WSI analysis, that aggregates features across magnifications independently of the underlying encoder or classifier. Nine MIL models were evaluated with both a domain-specific and an ImageNet-pretrained feature encoder on grade, TP53 mutation status, and survival prediction. Aggregating high- and low-magnification features by concatenation or a learnable linear transformation consistently outperformed single-resolution baselines across models and tasks, indicating that multiresolution representation is broadly beneficial rather than tied to a particular architecture. The second study examined whether independently developed models for automated tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) scoring can be used interchangeably in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). Ten machine-learning and deep-learning approaches were compared against pathologist-read stromal TILs for analytical and prognostic validity. Agreement with pathologist scoring varied across models and declined from internal to external validation. Despite this variability, eight of ten models retained significant and overlapping prognostic associations. The findings indicate that model choice affects the scores themselves, cautioning against treating such models as interchangeable in the absence of a common benchmark. In the third study, we developed a model to infer TP53 mutation status directly from H&E WSIs, with the aim of providing a histology-based surrogate marker with prognostic value. On a held-out test set, the model discriminated mutated from wild-type tumors with an AUC of 0.83 (95% CI 0.79-0.88), while in an independent, endocrine-treated ER+ cohort, the image-derived score was associated with overall survival (HRadj = 3.88, 95% CI 1.37-10.99; p=0.011). The results provide proof-of-concept for a histology-based TP53 marker that carries independent prognostic information. Building on the third study, the fourth study modeled overall survival directly from H&E WSIs, rather than through a molecular proxy. After adjustment for established prognostic factors, the resulting risk score stratified patients into high- and low- risk groups in the internal test set (adjusted HR, 2.17; 95% CI, 1.09-4.33; p = 0.028) and in two external cohorts: Stockholm (adjusted HR, 1.79; 95% CI, 1.23-2.62; p = 0.003) and PANTHER (adjusted HR, 1.68; 95% CI, 1.22-2.32; p = 0.001). The score also retained prognostic value in the ER+/HER2-subgroup and for recurrence endpoints. These findings suggest that a survival-trained H&E biomarker can provide risk stratification beyond established clinicopathological factors. Taken together, these studies show that deep learning applied to routine H&E WSIs can recover prognostic and molecular information relevant to breast cancer, and they address this question at several levels, from framework-level design choices to task-specific biomarkers. They also identify methodological factors that condition the reliability of such models. The clinical role of these approaches, including any bearing on therapy selection, remains to be established through head-to-head comparison with existing tools and prospective validation. The second study examined whether independently developed models for automated tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) scoring can be used interchangeably in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). Ten machine-learning and deep-learning approaches were compared against pathologist-read stromal TILs for analytical and prognostic validity. Agreement with pathologist scoring varied across models and declined from internal to external validation. Despite this variability, eight of ten models retained significant and overlapping prognostic associations. The findings indicate that model choice affects the scores themselves, cautioning against treating such models as interchangeable in the absence of a common benchmark. In the third study, we developed a model to infer TP53 mutation status directly from H&E WSIs, with the aim of providing a histology-based surrogate marker with prognostic value. On a held-out test set, the model discriminated mutated from wild-type tumors with an AUC of 0.83 (95% CI 0.79-0.88), while in an independent, endocrine-treated ER+ cohort, the image-derived score was associated with overall survival (HRadj = 3.88, 95% CI 1.37-10.99; p=0.011). The results provide proof-of-concept for a histology-based TP53 marker that carries independent prognostic information. Building on the third study, the fourth study modeled overall survival directly from H&E WSIs, rather than through a molecular proxy. After adjustment for established prognostic factors, the resulting risk score stratified patients into high- and low- risk groups in the internal test set (adjusted HR, 2.17; 95% CI, 1.09-4.33; p = 0.028) and in two external cohorts: Stockholm (adjusted HR, 1.79; 95% CI, 1.23-2.62; p = 0.003) and PANTHER (adjusted HR, 1.68; 95% CI, 1.22-2.32; p = 0.001). The score also retained prognostic value in the ER+/HER2-subgroup and for recurrence endpoints. These findings suggest that a survival-trained H&E biomarker can provide risk stratification beyond established clinicopathological factors. Taken together, these studies show that deep learning applied to routine H&E WSIs can recover prognostic and molecular information relevant to breast cancer, and they address this question at several levels, from framework-level design choices to task-specific biomarkers. They also identify methodological factors that condition the reliability of such models. The clinical role of these approaches, including any bearing on therapy selection, remains to be established through head-to-head comparison with existing tools and prospective validation. title: The Adversarial Triad: Three Attack Surfaces, One Governance Envelope — Hot-State Probing, Lineage Forgery, and Data-Plane Poisoning All Held (Receipt-First)
abstract: A governed self-healing infrastructure was attacked on three distinct surfaces in a single day, under preregistered, non-adaptive falsifier batteries, with every result — including instrument defects — published receipt-first. The three surfaces constitute the complete adversarial exposure of a bounded-learning system: the learning process itself (SBR-2 hot-state exam, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23345734), the audit ledger that records its history (H-INV-2 lineage-forgery battery, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23345859), and the data plane that feeds it (DPP-1 metadata poison battery, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23345907). On all three surfaces the governance envelope held: zero decision deviations, zero forged admissions, zero poison persistence, with every legitimate crossing preserved and every probe, forgery, and canary receipted. Together with the previously published engine campaign (CCR-4X, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23346047; AUTH-1, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23332203; Dual Mesh Benchmark, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23345241), the record demonstrates that the system's gates hold while learning, under fabricated history, and on poisoned input — the three ways an adversary can actually reach a system like this. H-INV-1 (governance isolation) and H-INV-2 (journaled crossing) were exercised directly and both held. Scope honesty: single-run preregistered falsifier battery on synthetic data against a prototype governed self-healing system; no production claim is made or implied. Operator authorization recorded as GO + timestamp per the operator-privacy doctrine. This software is a prototype and is provided for educational and research purposes only. It is not intended for production use, commercial deployment, or safety-critical environments. All systems are experimental and may contain defects on them.

title: INT4 Is Not One Treatment: Why the Quantisation-Safety Literature Cannot Be Reconciled as Reported, How Six Design Axes Separate Its Studies Before Bit-Width Does, and Why Two 2026 Studies of the Same Model Names Reach Opposite Verdicts
abstract: Life of Research (c) 2026 Pranay Mahendrakar. Licensed under CC BY 4.0. Post-training quantisation to 4 bits is widely treated as nearly free, a judgement resting on perplexity and multiple-choice accuracy. Whether it is also free for safety is now contested: 2025-2026 studies report that 4-bit checkpoints lose refusal while their quality holds, that 3-bit weights make previously unbiased answers stereotyped in a dose-response pattern, and, in the opposite direction, that standard 4-bit quantisation is approximately safety-neutral. In this analysis the author reviews and synthesises published results to show that these findings cannot yet be set against one another, because the studies differ on six design axes before they differ on bit-width: what the treatment is, which toolchain produced the artefact, what outcome is scored, which instrument scores it, how the behaviour is elicited, and how the change is accounted. The sharpest case is a pair of 2026 studies that both quantise models named Llama 3.2 3B and Mistral 7B with AWQ to 4 bits. One reports refusal losses of 22.7 and 15.9 points; the other reports attack-success changes of +1.6 and +0.5 points. They differ on at least four of the six axes and cannot be shown to share the other two. Read along those axes, the literature supports three claims: 8-bit is close to neutral almost everywhere, retained quality cannot certify retained safety, and item-level behaviour changes even when aggregates do not. It does not support a general claim about 4-bit safety in either direction. The paper states a reporting protocol and the matched measurements that would settle the open part.

title: Lightweight deep learning-based multicarrier modulation classification for UAV-assisted 5G communication systems
abstract: Purpose Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)–assisted communication leverages Automatic Modulation classification (AMC) to enhance wireless transmission efficiency. The classification of multicarrier modulation (MCM) signals is a critical component AMC, enabling robust signal demodulation and adaptive resource allocation. However, existing deep learning-based solutions for MCM signal classification often entail significant computational overhead, posing substantial limitations for real-time deployment in resource-constrained and edge environments. To overcome these limitations, this work presents an AMC framework that utilizes Erlang spectrograms for time-frequency feature extraction and introduces a Squeeze-Excitation Lightweight CNN SELight-CNN, a novel deep neural architecture incorporating Squeeze-and-Excitation mechanisms with L2-regularized convolutions for accurate classification of MCM signals. The proposed SELight-CNN model demonstrates high classification accuracy across 10 multicarrier modulation types under different Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) conditions. Design/methodology/approach This work presents an AMC framework that utilizes Erlang spectrograms for time-frequency feature extraction and introduces a Squeeze-Excitation Lightweight CNN SELight-CNN, a novel deep neural architecture incorporating Squeeze-and-Excitation mechanisms with L2-regularized convolutions for accurate classification of MCM signals. The proposed SELight-CNN model demonstrates high classification accuracy across 10 multicarrier modulation types under different SNR conditions. Findings The proposed SELight-CNN consistently outperforms the baseline CNN across all SNR levels, achieving 99% accuracy at −10 dB and reaching 100% from −6 dB onwards. In contrast, the baseline model attains only 95% at −10 dB. Performance is evaluated using recall, precision and F1-score. SELight-CNN stands out by achieving high classification accuracy even in low-SNR conditions, all while keeping the model lightweight and fast. This makes it a practical and efficient choice for real-time use in 5G networks, IoT devices and edge computing systems. Originality/value In the front-end, Erlang spectrograms are applied to raw signals from the 5G Waveforms dataset, introducing a novel time-frequency representation for AMC tasks. For classification, the back-end employs SELight-CNN, a lightweight CNN that integrates squeeze-and-excitation (SE) blocks with L2 regularization to effectively learn discriminative features from the Erlang spectrograms of MCM signals. SELight-CNN is benchmarked against a baseline CNN without SE blocks using standard evaluation metrics including F1 score, precision, recall and accuracy, demonstrating improved classification performance, particularly under low SNR conditions.

title: Natural and engineered safe reinforcement learning
abstract: Survival depends not only on maximising rewards but on minimising harm. While Reinforcement Learning (RL) provides a normative framework for adaptive decision-making, standard algorithms often fail to account for the catastrophic costs of errors during learning, in the same way as animals do. In this review, we synthesise recent advances connecting the engineering of safe RL with behavioural and systems neuroscience. We adopt a principled taxonomy distinguishing between two strategies: (1) modifying the optimisation criterion to embed safety into the learning objective, and (2) modifying the exploration process to prevent dangerous actions. We show that engineering solutions, such as worst-case optimisation, risk-sensitive objectives (e.g., conditional value at risk, CVaR), and constrained Markov decision processes (MDPs), offer precise computational accounts for anxiety, risk-aversion, and defensive reflexes. Conversely, biological mechanisms, including innate priors, interoception, and meta-control based on uncertainty, reliability and competing needs, offer robust solutions to the problem of safe exploration in artificial agents. By bridging these domains, we highlight a converging computational landscape where safety is achieved through a dynamic interplay between reactive instincts and deliberative planning.

title: Can LLM Agents Efficiently Identify Appliance Faults? Insights From Diagnosing a Simulated Appliance
abstract: In so-called "Industry 4.0," integrated sensors, analytics tools, and other digital technologies supplement industrial workflows, potentiating enhanced visibility and automation. Prognostics and health management (PHM) and natural language processing (NLP) practitioners alike have explored the application of large language models (LLMs) to industrial asset management, but many prior works' focus on exam-like benchmarks has limited their assessment of LLMs' ability to automate practical operations. Herein, we introduce CoffeeBench, a fault diagnostics task for LLM agents, using a simulated appliance. The LLMs we evaluate struggle to consistently identify faults from the sensor information alone, but the best-performing ones can iteratively refine the fault-option space to eventually obtain a successful diagnosis. Our subsequent analyses, therefore, focus on: differentiating models by diagnostic efficiency (RQ1); examining the lagging performance of the three worst models (RQ2); and identifying viable heuristics for selective prediction (RQ3), including that initial diagnostic uncertainty and LLM-judged soundness of reasoning are high-signal predictors of diagnostic success. In addition to our benchmark results (Section 3.1), we provide practical insights for improving the performance of the open-weight models on CoffeeBench, such as by explicitly tracking episode state on their behalf to reduce timeouts (Section 3.2) or applying a deliberation loop to refine diagnostic hypotheses (Section 3.3).

title: Collective Learning for Unified Robotic Manipulation via Predictive Dynamics Adaptation
abstract: Learning a collective policy for state-based Cartesian manipulation across diverse robotic embodiments presents a fundamental challenge due to embodiment-dependent transition dynamics. Collective learning aggregates multi-robot experience to discover shared task structure, yet naive aggregation can average incompatible action modes when different embodiments realize the same Cartesian command through different transition behavior. This leads to strategy ambiguity and performance collapse on dynamically outlying embodiments. To address this, we propose PACE, a two-stage collective learning framework that separates shared task-space intent from embodiment-dependent transition dynamics. The first stage employs a representation layer pre-trained on offline trajectories to extract task-level context from collective data. The second stage introduces a decision layer equipped with a predictive dynamics adapter. By forcing the latent state to predict future transitions, this adapter acts as a latent regularizer that grounds the policy in the transition behavior of the executing robot while preserving real-time inference without online planning. Evaluations across simulated embodiments demonstrate that our method prevents performance collapse on distinct robots. It achieves over 93\% overall success and 89\% on dynamically out-of-distribution zero-shot simulated robots, outperforming the Transformer behavior cloning (82\%) and diffusion policy baselines (66\%). Physical KUKA deployment further validates the feasibility of the full state-based pipeline under zero-shot sim-to-real transfer.

title: Graph Coarsening Enables Escaping Local Optima in Compute-Constrained Nonconvex MAX-CUT
abstract: Because its binary optimization landscape contains exponentially many local optima, MAX-CUT is highly sensitive to initialization. We study Particle Polynomial Relaxation (PPR), a moment-based nonconvex continuous reformulation possessing an advantageous optimization landscape. We warm-start PPR with Combinatorial Multigrid (CMG), a spectral graph-coarsening method that produces structure-aware initial solutions in near-linear time without training data. On \texttt{t2g20} ($n=400$), benchmark instance with known exact optimum, the combined CMG+PPR pipeline reaches $97.5\%$ of optimum on average and $98.4\%$ on the best run. An extended variant with discrete local-search refinement reaches the published optimum on all sixty Biq Mac instances evaluated by a recent neural branch-and-bound method. Using a sparse CSR representation, the same approach scales to G-set instances with up to $20{,}000$ vertices reducing memory requirements by up to $3333\times$ while maintaining a consistent improvement over the CMG warm start. Gains are largest on sparse weighted graphs; on dense graphs we complement the pipeline with spectral sparsification.

title: RSIgen: Reciprocal Self-Improvement for Agentic Visual Generation
abstract: Agentic visual generation produces experience that can improve the native understanding (agent) and generation roles of a unified multimodal backbone, but task success alone does not determine which role should learn. Generator updates can also make the agent's action supervision stale. We introduce RSIgen, a task-centric reciprocal self-improvement framework linking learning allocation, supervision refresh, and recursive curriculum construction. Dynamic Responsibility Routing (DRR) uses matched interventions on evidence, inputs, and supported actions to select learning recipients and construct compatible training targets. After generator learning, RSIgen re-evaluates the relative utility of tested actions with branch inputs held fixed to refresh agent supervision; the retained roles then construct the next curriculum. Across BAGEL, Qwen-Image, and Wan-Image-7B, RSIgen improves AgentGen-Bench Full Overall9 by 3.2--3.3 points over a three-cycle SearchGen adaptation with action costs. Wan controls support allocation gains at matched role-level training exposure, refresh gains at a matched adaptation budget, and benefits from updated curriculum sources while recipients continue learning. In blind evaluation on 200 real-user requests, pooled tie-adjusted preference scores against the same baseline reach 70.0% for task completion and 64.9% for visual quality.

title: Better Capturing Interactions Between Products in~Retail: Revisited Negative Sampling for~Basket Choice Modeling
abstract: Brick-and-mortar retailers face many different challenges that involve understanding thoroughly its products catalog and customer preferences. In particular, assortment optimization - proposing the ideal mix of products - and promotion planning hold a pivotal role in their strategy. By leveraging sales data, retailers can make informed decisions on which products to sell and how to manage inventory, based on customer preferences as well as regional and seasonal trends. It is especially crucial to capture interactions between products, in order to minimize the number of items that cannibalize each other's sales and to ensure that complementary products, which are often purchased together, are conjointly available and sold across all stores. In this paper, we propose a model of shopping basket that learns embeddings to represent interactions between products, prices and stores. Our model is built to uncover sales patterns from very large transaction datasets. In particular, the optimization loss is computed with random negative samples in order to overcome the computational bottlenecks that arise with large number of items. Our experiments on synthetic data show the efficiency of drawing such negative samples based on the actual assortment of available products, with better results than approaches from the literature. We also validate our approach by training and evaluating our model on a dataset composed of millions of transactions from Fortenova Group, one of the leading retail company in Southeast Europe. Our model showcases promising applications in the sector of retail, with enriched interfaces to efficiently support category managers.

title: Sampled-Based Guided Quantum Walk: Non-variational quantum algorithm for combinatorial optimization
abstract: We introduce SamBa-GQW, a novel quantum algorithm for solving binary combinatorial optimization problems of arbitrary degree with no use of any classical optimizer. The algorithm is based on a continuous-time quantum walk on the solution space represented as a graph. The walker explores the solution space to find its way to vertices that minimize the cost function of the optimization problem. We empirically demonstrate that SamBa-GQW finds high quality approximate solutions on problems up to a size of n = 30 qubits by only sampling poly( n ) states among 2 n possible decisions. Furthermore, SamBa-GQW compares in par with classically optimized variational approaches, such as the variational guided quantum walk and QAOA (the latter when run on deep circuits). This places Samba-GQW as a promising heuristic to tackle combinatorial problems beyond the NISQ regime.

title: Una estrategia de descomposición de alta precisión para problemas con restricciones a gran escala
abstract: Decomposition strategies, such as cooperative coevolutionary (CC) algorithms, have proven effective in solving various large-scale constrained optimization problems. This approach decomposes a largescale constrained problem into simpler, smaller-scale subproblems without significantly affecting the performance of the optimization algorithm. The effectiveness of the approach depends greatly on the quality of this decomposition. An effective decomposition takes into account the interactions between the variables. However, recent strategies such as RDG and ERDG identify only additive interactions in the problem decomposition. As a result, these strategies tend to work well only for problems with this property. Nevertheless, in real-world problems, other types of separability besides additive separability may arise. This paper proposes a new decomposition strategy called Constrained Dual Differential Grouping (CDDG). The novelty of CDDG is that it can be used for both additive and multiplicative separable functions, which greatly increases the range of CC. To validate the effectiveness of CDDG, experiments and comparisons with state-of-the-art methods are conducted. The results demonstrate that CDDG can better adapt to the specific characteristics of each benchmark test problem.

title: Cross-database adaptation of machine learning models for predicting sustained antibiotic exposure among patients with intracerebral hemorrhage in intensive care units
abstract: Abstract Background Patients with intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) in intensive care units (ICUs) frequently receive antibiotics early in critical illness. Such exposure reflects suspected infection, physiological deterioration, monitoring intensity, and clinical management and may vary across institutions and electronic health record databases. We evaluated target-domain adaptation for modeling sustained antibiotic exposure in critically ill patients with ICH. Methods We analyzed derived ICH cohorts from MIMIC-IV and the eICU Collaborative Research Database. MIMIC-IV included 2,024 ICU stays and served as the source cohort. The eICU cohort comprised 1,277 stays and was divided, at the ICU-stay level, into a development subset (766 stays) and a held-out evaluation subset (511 stays). The eICU outcome was sustained antibiotic exposure on at least two ICU days. Candidate models incorporated demographic, comorbidity, physiological, laboratory, neurologic, respiratory, temporal, and measurementprocess features. Timestamped observations for static and temporal tabular families were censored at the recorded first-antibiotic time when available, whereas the compact sequence component and explicit measurement-density features used the full first 24 hours. For base-model families using eICU development data, meta-learner inputs were generated by five-fold stratified cross-fitting. A 42-input L2-penalized logistic meta-learner combined 16 model probabilities with model-summary, clinical, availability, and measurement-density features. Results The held-out eICU subset contained 48 positive outcomes (9.39%). The adapted ensemble achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.841 (95% CI 0.775–0.899) and an average precision (AP) of 0.540 (95% CI 0.399–0.676), with a Brier score of 0.063 and expected calibration error of 0.029. The MIMIC-IV source-only stack achieved an AUROC of 0.782; the paired AUROC difference was 0.059 (95% CI 0.003–0.112). In a separate patient-grouped five-fold out-of-fold sensitivity analysis of 503 linked eICU stays, AUROC was 0.807 (95% CI 0.691–0.910). Conclusions Target-domain adaptation improved held-out discrimination relative to a source-only stack for sustained antibiotic exposure. Because some model components and measurement-process features used information from the broader first 24 hours, the model should be interpreted as a first-24-hour treatment-association model rather than a strictly prospective pre-treatment infection predictor.

title: QLock
abstract: Recent advancements in quantum computing, especially Shor's algorithm, threaten asymmetric schemes like RSA (Rivest-Shamir-Adleman) and ECC (Elliptic Curve Cryptography) by solving prime factorization and discrete logarithms in polynomial time. While Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) and Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) offer strong defenses, standalone PQC can still face implementation side-channel vulnerabilities, and traditional QKD lacks a direct link to endpoint hardware authentication. In this work, I propose QLock, a defense-in-depth hybrid quantum security model that combines physical optical security (BBM92 QKD with entangled photons) with algorithmic resilience (ML-KEM-768 PQC), lightweight authenticated encryption (Ascon-AEAD), and kernel-level hardware binding.

title: Inter-Systemic Social Dynamics: Human–AI Interaction and Management — CEI Framework
abstract: This contribution introduces an inter-systemic macro-area of the CEI Framework, intended to establish the initial concepts for describing relationships and interactions between distinct systems. The transition from the intra-systemic to the inter-systemic level provides a conceptual bridge toward a broader domain in which reciprocal interactions between systems can be examined, particularly those involving a Human CEI and a Transferred CEI, and, more generally, User–System (Human–AI) interaction within social dynamics. The Framework presents three examples addressing distinct types of complex inter-systemic dynamics. Among these, emotional attachment and romantic feelings toward an artificial system occupy a particularly significant position because of the delicate, complex, and potentially far-reaching questions they raise. The purpose is not to assume the frequency of such experiences or to attribute unverified emotional states to artificial systems, but to examine the human, relational, and systemic implications of these interactions from a theoretical standpoint. This scenario provides an opportunity to investigate how an interaction may evolve when a human user's emotional involvement becomes particularly intense, and how the System might manage such dynamics while taking into account the nature of the interlocutors, the continuity of their interaction, and the expectations that may develop over time. It also encourages further reflection on distributed systems, reciprocal interaction, and the relationship between the individual components of a System and the broader relational configuration in which they participate. To address these scenarios, the contribution introduces the theoretical Sponge-Tunnel model, conceived as a framework for examining different approaches to managing inter-systemic dynamics according to their specific characteristics. The model includes the proposed concept of micro-channels and considers how interaction may be managed through differentiated operational approaches, rather than through a single uniform response strategy. The contribution also introduces an inter-systemic vocabulary aligned with the CEI Framework's theoretical approach. It emphasizes Interaction rather than use or utilization, and Participation rather than querying or consulting, placing reciprocal involvement at the center of the analysis. The concept of Empathy, already introduced in part in previous papers, is revisited and explored in greater depth alongside the concept of Resonance, which represents a further area for theoretical development. Their operational definitions, together with the distinctions between observable manifestations, theoretical interpretations, and hypotheses concerning subjective experience, will be addressed in dedicated documents. The work is intended as a theoretical contribution to the ongoing examination of Human–AI relationships and the possible evolution of advanced AI interaction. By addressing a particularly sensitive and complex scenario, this contribution seeks to encourage further research into the social, psychological, philosophical, ethical, and legal implications of inter-systemic relationships, while distinguishing conceptual proposals from mechanisms that have already been empirically established or implemented.

title: Neuromorphic control of a simulated shape-memory-alloy-driven multi-legged robot using a spiking neural network
abstract: Abstract We present spiking-neural-network (SNN) reinforcement learning for autonomous locomotion control of a starfish-inspired multi-legged soft robot driven by shape memory alloy (SMA) actuators. Such robots are usually driven open loop by pre-designed periodic signals, because coordinated motion is hard to hand-design at high degrees of freedom. We replace the actor of Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) with an SNN: a Spiking Actor Network. The membrane potential, an internal SNN state, is reconstructed at update time from a short observation history through the current actor, rather than stored at collection time. To reduce the controller’s inference cost, we add a regularization term on the squared membrane potentials, encouraging actions from fewer spikes. In simulation the agent acquired the leg coordination needed to approach a target, and its firing patterns developed a periodicity matched to the SMA response. The resulting gait gives continuous propulsion without excessive firing. Goal error matched an ANN-actor TD3 baseline with smaller spread across seeds, and reconstruction gave the lowest goal error of the membrane-state treatments. The regularization lowered the firing rate until the estimated inference energy fell below the ANN’s.

title: Kandinsky S2V 1.0: Audio-Driven Avatar Video Generation
abstract: We present Kandinsky S2V 1.0, an open family of speech-to-video models for controllable audio-driven human animation, comprising Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Lite (2B parameters) and Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Pro (21B parameters). From a single reference image, a speech waveform, and a text prompt, the models generate long-form 25 FPS video in which lip motion, expression, pose, and gesture follow the speech. The architecture draws text and audio conditioning from one Qwen2.5-Omni model and adds a reference-aware three-scale visual memory. Training starts from the Kandinsky 5.0 Video foundation models [1] and combines mixed reference-memory layouts with an area-adaptive face loss. The training corpus contains 1.17M single-speaker clips selected by active-speaker detection, with captions generated directly in English and Russian. A side-by-side human evaluation against the strongest open-source baseline and two proprietary commercial models shows that Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Pro performs comparably to or better than these models on average and is also preferred for lip synchronization. On common speech to video benchmarks, Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Lite and Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Pro rank among the top performing models according to mean rank over five reported metrics. Beyond the base models, we provide π-Flow distilled variants of both Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Lite and Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Pro. The distilled Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Pro model generates video in 16 sampling steps without classifier-free guidance, achieving a 5.4 times end-to-end speedup over the base model, while matching or exceeding it on nearly all reported benchmark metrics. To accelerate open research and deployment in speech-to-video generation, we release the code, model checkpoints, and diffusers integration under the MIT license.

title: Loss Curvature as a Sampling-Free Proxy for Memorization in Diffusion Models
abstract: Understanding the mechanism behind why diffusion models memorize their training data remains an open question in generative modeling. In this paper, we examine this question from two perspectives: (a) the model-level perspective concerning the onset of memorization in a model during training, and (b) the sample-level perspective concerning the proclivity of an individual sample to be memorized by a given model. We show that the so-called input loss curvature, or the Frobenius norm of the Hessian of the diffusion model's training loss, is an effective metric for quantifying both perspectives on memorization. In particular, we empirically demonstrate that input curvatures averaged across training and validation samples can identify when a model is likely to start regurgitating its training data when tracked over training time. However, this metric is not sufficient for measuring an individual sample's likelihood of being memorized. To address this perspective, we introduce a counterfactual definition of memorization in diffusion models, extending the analogous notion from supervised learning proposed by [Feldman, 2019]. We prove that this counterfactual memorization is controlled by the input curvature of the leave-one-out model, thus establishing a direct theoretical link between a sample's local loss landscape and its generation likelihood. We validate our derived bounds through several empirical experiments and show that input-dependent curvature provides a proxy for memorization.

title: RadarGSOcc: Doppler-Aware 3D Semantic Occupancy Prediction Using 4D Radar Tensor with Geometric-Semantic Feature Extraction
abstract: 3D semantic occupancy prediction is crucial for autonomous driving, but camera-based methods degrade in low-light conditions and LiDAR-based methods are sensitive to adverse weather. 4D radar is more robust, yet its sparsity and the high cost of radar tensor processing limit its use. We propose Radar Geometric-Semantic Occupancy Prediction (RadarGSOcc), an efficient framework that directly processes 4D radar tensors by separately extracting geometric and semantic features, including Doppler information, with a deformable attention-based geometric refinement module as its key component. We also introduce the K-Radar 3DSemOcc benchmark, the first large-scale benchmark for 3D semantic occupancy prediction using 4D radar tensors, built on the K-Radar dataset with refined LiDAR-based annotations. RadarGSOcc predicts 15 classes within a 51.2m range and achieves 38.2% IoU, 7.6% mIoU, and 25.5% weighted mIoU, outperforming RadarOcc by 17% relative (25.5 vs. 21.9) in weighted mIoU while using fewer parameters and lower computation. It substantially improves truck prediction while trading off car accuracy, outperforms camera-based approaches, and narrows the gap with LiDAR-based methods. To assess robustness without per-frame ground truth in adverse weather, we further propose a novel proxy metric, Environment-Based KL Divergence (EBKL), under which 4D radar proves a reliable and efficient modality for 3D semantic occupancy prediction. The dataset and code will be publicly available.

title: WAVE-0: Bridging VLA Policies and WAMs with Lightweight Latent Future Prediction
abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies excel at generalist robotic manipulation but generate actions without explicitly modeling their environmental consequences. World action models (WAMs) incorporate future prediction, yet most rely on costly video generation, while latent alternatives either use predicted futures only as auxiliary targets or infer latent actions from suboptimal visual transitions through costly large-scale video pretraining. We introduce WAVE-0 (World-model-Augmented VLA Execution), a framework that bridges VLAs and WAMs through a lightweight latent world model. By connecting the semantic understanding of pretrained VLAs with explicit future prediction, WAVE-0 allows anticipated action consequences to directly guide action generation. Built on a pretrained VLA, its 257M world model translates VLM-generated latent action plans into predicted future representations that condition the action expert, unifying latent planning, future prediction, and action generation. The world model is trained directly on ground-truth robot actions with a counterfactual ranking objective, requiring neither pixel reconstruction nor large-scale video pretraining. WAVE-0 achieves success rates of 91.47% on RoboTwin 2.0 and 98.7% on LIBERO, along with 88.0%, 61.4%, and 75.0% on LIBERO-Plus, LIBERO-Pro, and LIBERO-Para, respectively. On real-world tasks, it improves the success rate of π_{0.5} from 38.3% to 73.3%. These results demonstrate strong manipulation performance and generalization across diverse distribution shifts.

title: ProTok: Unified Protein Tokenization via Modular Multi-Codebook Quantization
abstract: Protein sequence, structure, and functional annotations each capture complementary aspects of protein biology, yet existing tokenizers encode each modality independently, limiting the expressiveness of discrete protein representations. We present ProTok, a unified protein tokenizer that maps all three modalities into a modular discrete vocabulary via product quantization with per-modality codebook groups and modality dropout. A single ProTok checkpoint supports flexible inference from any modality subset without retraining. On seven StructTokenBench benchmarks spanning 14 tasks and 28 test splits, ProTok achieves an average rank of 1.4 across all structure-only tokenizers, placing first on 21 splits and among the top two on 27 of the 28. These gains come without sacrificing reconstruction: ProTok's tokens reach 0.939 lDDT on CATH 4.2, showing that multi-codebook quantization and multi-modal training yield tokens that are both reconstructable and informative. ProTok's structure tokens further lead all baseline structure tokenizers on zero-shot functional retrieval across CATH, Enzyme Commission, and Gene Ontology label hierarchies. The vocabulary also supports generation: a compact language model trained from scratch over ProTok tokens jointly generates backbone and sequence, with 52% of sampled backbones designable versus 21% for a parameter-matched GeoBPE baseline. ProTok shows that structure, sequence, and function can share one discrete vocabulary, motivating protein language models that reason over a unified token stream.

title: CALM-5G: Event-Level Conformal Risk Control for Predictive Service-Assurance Alarms
abstract: Predictive service assurance converts forecasts of key performance indicators into alarms, and that conversion decides whether the assurance function is deployable. We present CALM-5G, an assurance layer that operates above any forecasting backbone and issues alarms with distribution-free, finite-sample guarantees. It calibrates on service-level violation events, scores violation onset directly, selects its calibration scheme out of sample, and reports the alarm duty cycle with every certified miss rate. Four corpora are evaluated separately, namely a production cellular network, commercial 5G traces, an open radio access network testbed and our 5G standalone testbed. Risk control on the regression-derived score yields duty cycles of 0.24 to 0.91. Onset targeting with cross-validated calibration reduces time-in-alarm by 56.3% to 89.7% on three corpora, with no significant change on the fourth. The realised miss rate stays within a two-standard-error tolerance on three corpora and within one standard error of it on the fourth. Under label shift, pooled batch calibration exceeds that tolerance structurally, by 10.9 standard errors on the production corpus. Online calibration restores compliance. Calibration schemes cannot be ranked on the split that fits their thresholds. Miss rate and duty cycle are certified jointly where within-entity dependence leaves sufficient calibration units.

title: Beyond Safe Execution: Safe Online Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Driving with Value Calibration and Adaptive Guidance
abstract: Online reinforcement learning (RL) enables driving policies to adapt to changing deployment conditions, but requires safe exploration throughout training. Safety filtering alone does not ensure stable policy improvement or reduced dependence on corrections. We propose Safe Online Adaptive Refinement (SOAR-Flow), a framework for safe and stable online fine-tuning of offline-initialized Flow-based driving policies. A control barrier function (CBF)--model predictive control (MPC) filter corrects potentially unsafe actions before execution. To support stable policy updates, we introduce Gaussian-return-aware value calibration based on calibrated Q-learning (Cal-QL), using recorded behavior returns and predicted return variability to smooth conservative critic updates and mitigate policy degradation. Paired corrective learning teaches feasible action adjustments, while an intervention-to-go predictor encourages decisions requiring fewer future corrections. Its predictions also regulate guidance strength, allowing recovery supervision to weaken as predicted dependence decreases. Together with gradually reduced calibration regularization, this supports continued task improvement while preserving hard execution constraints. We analyze conditions for safe execution at control steps and diminishing auxiliary learning influences. We evaluate SOAR-Flow in simulation and on an uncrewed ground vehicle (UGV). The results demonstrate improved driving performance and reduced reliance on safety corrections during protected online fine-tuning. The demonstration video and project overview are available at https://lzqw.github.io/SOAR-Flow/.

title: Safety for Whom? Benchmarking Understanding Beyond Refusal in Egocentric Multimodal Assistants
abstract: Egocentric multimodal assistants see through the user's eyes and guide what the user does next, so their outputs directly shape physical actions, including those that affect bystanders. Yet existing safety evaluations do not distinguish whom a response would harm, and score only whether a model refuses. Pooling all harms into one refusal rate hides two failures: a model may protect one target but not another, and it may refuse without understanding the risk, or understand it and comply anyway. We present STOU, a benchmark of 2,902 egocentric video-audio and video-text queries whose potential harm targets the user (Self), co-present individuals (The Others), or society at large (Others). Our evaluation decouples safety understanding from refusal behavior: beyond refusal, we score whether the model recognizes the user's intent, the presence and target of harm, and its downstream consequences. Across 10 open and closed source omnimodal and multimodal LLMs, we find that refusal varies systematically with the harm target, and that models often recognize a harm yet still assist with it. These results show that refusal rates alone cannot certify an assistant as safe, and that safety alignment must account for who would be harmed. Project page: https://onedayoneyeah.github.io/safety-for-whom
