title: Mirror subspace diagonalization: a real-time quantum Krylov algorithm with near-optimal sampling cost
abstract: Quantum Krylov algorithms are a promising approach for ground-state energy estimation on near-term quantum computers. However, their sampling cost is inherently high because each Hamiltonian term is measured individually. Despite various mitigation techniques, this overhead remains a bottleneck for large-scale electronic structure problems. We introduce mirror subspace diagonalization (MSD), which approaches the theoretical lower bound on the sampling cost for quantum Krylov algorithms built upon real-time evolution. MSD uses a finite-difference formula to express the Hamiltonian as a linear combination of time-evolution unitaries with symmetrically shifted timesteps, enabling efficient estimation of the Hamiltonian matrix within the Krylov subspace. By optimizing the timestep and shifting the energy spectrum, finite-difference and statistical errors are minimized simultaneously, allowing MSD to attain the sampling-cost lower bound up to a logarithmic factor. We further apply classical post-processing to infer Hamiltonian moments, which mitigate the ground-state energy error via the Lanczos scheme. Our analysis shows MSD is particularly effective when the Hamiltonian’s spectral norm is much smaller than its 1-norm, as in high-accuracy molecular simulations with large basis sets and strong electronic correlations. Numerical results for various molecular models show sampling-cost reductions of roughly 10 to 10,000 times over the conventional quantum Krylov algorithm.

title: Low-resource Indigenous language translator
abstract: La línea de investigación presentada en este trabajo tiene como objetivo formular e implementar una metodología para la creación de traductores de lenguas con bajos recursos en América del Sur. El lenguaje forma parte de la cultura e identidad de las comunidades, especialmente en pueblos originarios. La globalización y la marginalización histórica, entre otros factores, provocaron que muchas lenguas se hayan retraído hasta desaparecer mientras que otras, se desvanecen. La metodología propuesta involucra la búsqueda, recolección y depuración de datos para la creación del corpus bitexto que permita la creación de modelos de lenguaje su cientemente ricos como para la implementación de máquinas de traducción basadas en Transformers. Las lenguas objeto de estudio con las que inicialmente se trabajará son el Kaingang y el Ayoreo. En cuanto a la primera, se ha empezado a aplicar la metodología conformando un pequeño corpus y se ha implementado un traductor basado en el esquema codi cador-decodi cador usando Transformers. Los resultados preliminares expuestos aquí permiten obtener algunas conclusiones útiles para la formulación de la metodología.

title: Designing Chinese Tokenizers under Data Constraints: A White-Box Empirical Study of Character Fragmentation
abstract: Chinese text requires substantially more tokens than English in large language models (LLMs), increasing API costs and context-window consumption. Most prior work measures this premium using off-the-shelf tokenizers, but the underlying mechanism—where the additional tokens actually arise—remains poorly understood, particularly under data-constrained training, which is common in domain-specific and small-scale models. We implement BPE, WordPiece, and Unigram from scratch (approximately 1,000 lines of standard-library code), train them on 20,000 Chinese news documents, and quantify per-character tokenization across vocabulary sizes from 8K to 128K. Characters are grouped by frequency, and evaluation uses a held-out test set with clustered-bootstrap confidence intervals. The central result is a low-frequency fragmentation effect: at an 8K vocabulary, byte-level BPE splits characters appearing fewer than 100 times in training into an average of 2.04 tokens per character, compared with 1.00 for high-frequency characters; enlarging the vocabulary 16-fold reduces this value to 1.10 at a fixed training scale. Comparison with production tokenizers reveals a spectrum from 2.24 (OpenAI's cl100k) and 2.04 (our 8K implementation) to 1.02 (DeepSeek's Chinese-optimized 128K vocabulary), indicating that the effect depends on vocabulary allocation and training scale rather than being an inherent property of Chinese. A semantic-equivalence experiment further supports this conclusion: for equivalent Chinese-English sentence pairs, an English-centric tokenizer uses 65% more tokens for Chinese, whereas a balanced byte-level BPE trained on 20,000 documents (10K Chinese + 10K English) uses 27% fewer. The paper concludes with configuration guidance for Chinese-focused tokenizers under data constraints.

title: Earthquakes: The USGS Feed, Magnitude 2.5 and Up
abstract: This paper documents Earthquakes, the Orbital Network layer that plots seismic events from the USGS earthquake feed — magnitude 2.5 and above worldwide — on the real-time globe, with each event's magnitude, depth, location and origin time taken from the named source. title: NativData Tech Project 1: Building a Domain-Specific Nigerian Pidgin Dataset for Fintech Customer Support Methods and Progress Report
abstract: This methods and progress report describes NativData Tech Project 1, an independent effort to build a structured Nigerian Pidgin English conversational dataset for fintech and mobile-banking customer support. Nigerian Pidgin is widely spoken, yet most AI systems used in Nigerian banking were not trained on it. The result is frequent misreading of intent, emotion and urgency in automated support. This project addresses that gap with a staged, annotated, audio-supported resource. The report covers: - the problem and project aims - high-level design (four progressive stages of complexity) - public-facing methodology (AI-assisted generation, automated checks, native-speaker review) - project roles - current progress (Stage 1 in development; audio aligned with approved text) - limitations and next steps Proprietary generation rules and the full dataset are not released in this report. Access for research or collaboration can be requested from the author. A companion geospatial analysis of Pidgin distribution and financial inclusion is published separately (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23042043).

title: AnesLLM — Anesthesia Decision Dataset
abstract: AnesLLM is a clinical decision-support benchmark for anesthesia. It contains intraoperative decision windows derived from VitalDB(https://vitaldb.net) from Seoul National University Hospital: everything observable before a decision, plus the action the clinician actually took and two consensus alternatives estimated from the actions of all clinicians in the cohort (supervised LightGBM, case-grouped out-of-fold predictions). - 3,168 cases · 84,813 decision windows - Splits: dev.zip (25) · train_*.zip (2,994) · test.zip (149) - 5 action classes: `increase_hypnotic`, `reduce_hypnotic`, `increase_opioid`, `reduce_opioid`, `no_action` (+ `vasopressor` as an option, never ground truth) Each window contains 280 variables(patient and surgery, preoperative laboratory tests, 10 min of vital signs, effect-site concentrations and a 20-min action history) preceding the decision, the action actually taken (five hypnotic and opioid titration classes) and two consensus actions reflecting what the cohort's anaesthetists usually do in similar clinical states. The dataset includes case-level partitions, a difficulty-stratified test partition, a data dictionary and audit reports on integrity, information leakage, plausibility, drift, missingness and privacy. It is designed to evaluate the ability of any artificial intelligence system to choose the next action in a real case, and its construction method can be applied to other automated anaesthesia records.

title: Stock Exchange Trading Optimization Algorithm Improved Based on Information Technology Investment Analysis for Numerical Optimization and Practical Problems
abstract: Stock Exchange Trading Optimization (SETO) is a population-based metaheuristic with a compact market-inspired search framework, but its performance may be limited by uneven random initialization, coarse Relative Strength Index-based search-state identification, and excessive concentration of trading resources. To address these limitations, this study proposes an improved SETO, termed ISETO, by reformulating concepts from information technology investment analysis into population-search mechanisms. First, an IT investment portfolio screening initialization strategy jointly considers solution quality and spatial diversity to improve initial population coverage. Second, a discounted-return and downside-risk dual-state search strategy evaluates the magnitude, temporal relevance, and risk of historical improvements to adaptively coordinate exploration and exploitation. Third, an entropy-regularized real-option capital reallocation strategy redistributes search resources according to solution quality, capital efficiency, technical debt, and population diversity, while reinvesting abandoned candidates into underexplored regions to mitigate stagnation. The dominant computational complexity remains approximately O(TmaxND). ISETO is evaluated on 22 benchmark functions from the IEEE CEC2020 and CEC2022 suites under 10- and 20-dimensional settings and compared with nine representative metaheuristic algorithms. Under the conventional iteration-based setting, ISETO achieves the best or tied-best mean results on all CEC2020 functions at both dimensions, all 12 CEC2022 functions at 10 dimensions, and 11 of the 12 CEC2022 functions at 20 dimensions. Additional experiments under an identical objective-function evaluation budget confirm that these advantages are not simply caused by additional function evaluations. Holm-adjusted statistical tests and Cliff’s delta effect sizes further support the significance and practical magnitude of the observed improvements. Ablation experiments verify that all three proposed mechanisms contribute positively, while parameter sensitivity and population-diversity analyses demonstrate that ISETO is relatively robust to parameter variation and better able to preserve exploration capability during evolution. The additional mechanisms introduce only a moderate runtime overhead relative to the original SETO. ISETO is further applied to a three-dimensional robotic-arm path-planning problem. Over 30 independent runs, it obtains a best objective value of 290.69 and a mean value of 291.91. Its best result is 5.56% lower than the best competing result, while its mean result improves upon the original SETO by approximately 6.02%. These results demonstrate that ISETO provides improved convergence accuracy, robustness, and search diversity while retaining competitive computational efficiency, and has promising potential for constrained engineering optimization.

title: From Efficiency to Sufficiency: The Cost-Aware Measurement Design Framework for Automated Essay Scoring
abstract: Compute cost in automated essay scoring (AES) is usually treated as a technical efficiency issue rather than a measurement design concern. Yet deployment decisions require more than reporting latency, model size, or inference expense. In high-stakes settings, total burden includes validation, monitoring, adjudication, compliance, and governance; in instructional settings, pricing, licensing, and integration may dominate cost. This paper reframes AES as a cost-constrained measurement system and introduces the Cost-Aware Measurement Design (CAMD) Framework, a four-layer structure consisting of metering, allocation, unit economics, and decision, for translating computational and workflow resource records into decision-relevant cost constructs. Direct cost is specified as monetary outlay plus attributable labor and time, and two criteria, design attribution and auditability, determine what the cost boundary excludes. Burdens that satisfy neither criterion, such as institutional capability and governance posture, are represented as constraints on which designs are admissible rather than priced. The paper defines cost per defensible score (CPDS) and argues that AES systems should be compared by quality-cost sufficiency: minimizing cost among defensible scoring designs that satisfy measurement requirements. Scoring volume conditions all four layers, so cost per defensible score is treated as a function of scale rather than as a single transferable number. CAMD provides a portable basis for representing, comparing, and evaluating cost across AES studies and deployment contexts.

The paper defines cost per defensible score (CPDS) and argues that AES systems should be compared by quality-cost sufficiency: minimizing cost among defensible scoring designs that satisfy measurement requirements. Scoring volume conditions all four layers, so cost per defensible score is treated as a function of scale rather than as a single transferable number. CAMD provides a portable basis for representing, comparing, and evaluating cost across AES studies and deployment contexts.

title: The Generalized BEADS Representation: An Informationally Complete Visualization of Mixed Quantum States
abstract: A deep understanding of quantum information theory is essential for quantum science and technology. However, quantum mechanics and particularly quantum information theory suffer from a lack of intuitive images. Visualization tools offer novel perspectives on many problems in quantum physics by revealing important properties of quantum states and processes that are otherwise obscured by abstract mathematical formalisms. Here, we extend the previously established BEADS representation of pure states to the so-called generalized BEADS representation of mixed quantum states. We introduce spherical functions, so-called beads to visualize correlation structures of mixed quantum states. A recursive optimization scheme is used to obtain minimum-entanglement pure state decompositions of all subsystems of a given N-qubit state. We show how correlation function components can be decomposed into individual contributions that directly correspond to different types of correlations of mixed states. This allows us to visually characterize the total correlation, genuine n-partite entanglement, nonclassical quantum-discord-type correlations as well as classical correlations. After outlining the mathematical details relevant for constructing the representation, we examine the generalized BEADS representations for various classes of mixed states including product, classically correlated, separable but nonclassically correlated, as well as entangled states. As exemplary applications of the generalized BEADS representation, we showcase entanglement distillation and the effects of noise channels.

title: Communicating Uncertainty in AI-Supported Nurse Scheduling: Expert Co-Design and Evaluation of an Explainable AI Prototype
abstract: Nurse scheduling is a complex optimization problem in which nurses are assigned to shifts to meet staffing demands while complying with working-time limits, qualification requirements, and other operational and regulatory constraints. Artificial intelligence is increasingly being used to support this process by forecasting future staffing needs and providing advice on how to improve shift scheduling. Effective human-AI collaboration in nurse scheduling requires users to understand, interpret, and appropriately act on AI forecasts and advice. However, it remains insufficiently understood how healthcare professionals use transparency mechanisms like uncertainty communication and AI advice explanations when making staffing decisions. Applying a human-centered design approach, we iteratively developed a prototype decision support system for nurse scheduling and evaluated it through a mixed-methods user study with expert users. Using thematic analysis, questionnaire data, and eye tracking, we examine how healthcare professionals interact with the system and how uncertainty communication and explanations of AI advice influence understanding, decision confidence, trust, and usability. We found that the uncertainty communicated in AI forecasts was frequently misinterpreted and reduced decision confidence. Explanations were generally perceived positively, but did not significantly affect decision confidence or advice acceptance. We conclude with eight design implications derived from our findings, providing insights for the design of more transparent and effective AI-supported decision support tools in healthcare.

title: MemoryVLN: From Ego-Aware Memory Representation to Cross-Context Memory Reuse in Vision-Language Navigation
abstract: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) have shown strong potential for embodied vision-language navigation (VLN), yet their performance degrades on long-horizon trajectories due to context-length limits, redundant historical observations, and unstable spatial alignment across time. These issues make it difficult to both compress long navigation histories and reliably reuse past spatial experience. To address these limitations, we propose \textbf{MemoryVLN}, a unified memory-driven navigation system built around memory construction and management. During memory construction, \emph{Long Sequence Compression} employs forgetting-curve-inspired temporal sampling to preserve dense recent evidence and sparse yet representative distant observations under a limited token budget. \emph{Ego-Aware Memory Representation} further integrates 2D semantic tokens, 3D geometric tokens, and 6D agent poses, allowing each memory to encode both what was observed and where it was observed. During memory management, \emph{Hierarchical Memory Bank} maintains in-episode and context-level memories through cross-context warm-start and confidence-controlled write-back. \emph{Memory Enhancement} then retrieves the Top-$K$ relevant memories according to the current navigation state and fuses them with the current visual tokens. Together, these mechanisms transform raw navigation history into compact, spatially grounded, selectively retrievable, and reusable navigation experience. Extensive experiments on R2R-CE and RxR-CE demonstrate consistent improvements over the state-of-the-art baselines by a substantial margin (i.e., 2\% and 6.5\% in successful rate).

title: How Reliable Are Large Language Models for Soil Organic Carbon Assessment? An Australian Benchmark
abstract: Soil organic carbon (SOC) is an indicator of agricultural soil condition and carbon storage, but numerical outputs from large language models (LLMs) require validation before use in monitoring or management. We evaluated seven general-purpose LLM configurations on three direct-response tasks: estimating 0--10 cm SOC concentrations for 308 Australian paddocks under two information conditions, calculating SOC stock in 120 matched scenarios, and comparing 300 paddock pairs. References were measured SOC records or deterministic calculations; response validity, repeated-call dispersion and estimated API cost were assessed separately. Additional measured soil attributes reduced concentration mean absolute error by 13--62\% across configurations, although high-SOC underprediction and paddock-specific errors persisted. Six configurations were highly accurate in stock calculations using equation-native units without coarse fragments, but accuracy declined with physically equivalent alternative units. Pairwise accuracy was 90.5--94.6\% overall and 59.1--70.9\% for 52 closely separated pairs; some configurations were sensitive to presentation order. Nearly all outputs were parseable, without necessarily being correct. The benchmark identifies three distinct requirements for AI-mediated SOC assessment: agreement with measured concentrations, unit-consistent stock calculations and reliable discrimination between sites. These findings support task-specific validation and auditable calculations, rather than unverified use of LLM outputs as ecological evidence.

title: HessFormer: Hessians at Foundation Scale
abstract: Abstract Whilst there have been major advancements in the field of first order optimisation of deep learning models, where state of the art open source mixture of expert models go into the hundreds of billions of parameters, methods that rely on Hessian vector products, are still limited to run on a single GPU and thus cannot even work for models in the billion parameter range. We release a software package HessFormer, which integrates nicely with the well known Transformers package and allows for distributed hessian vector computation across a single node with multiple GPUs. Underpinning our implementation is a distributed stochastic lanczos quadrature algorithm, which we release for public consumption. Using this package we investigate the Hessian spectral density of the recent Deepseek 70bn parameter model.

title: O USO DO MODELOS AMPLOS DE LINGUAGEM (LLM) PARA EXTRAÇÃO DE ESQUEMAS DE CONJUNTO DE DADOS SEMIESTRUTURADOS
abstract: A maioria dos dados gerados com a evolução da tecnologia não seguem um esquema definido, fazendo com que o uso de formatos flexíveis, como o JSON, tornem-se essenciais. Entretanto, a falta de padronização define desafios para trabalhar com esse tipo de documentos. Os esquemas são essenciais para aplicativos centrados em dados, porém, a identificação dos esquemas em dados semi-estruturados, onde os metadados se encontram nos próprios valores, possui dificuldades para realizar uma inferência automática. Esse trabalho propõe uma abordagem e avalia o desempenho de LLMs na extração de esquemas de fonte de dados não estruturados, focando em documentos legais. A metodologia possuí um fluxo preparatório para os documentos: coleta, pré-processamento e preparação dos dados. Após isso, é montado manualmente um golden schema para servir de referência na avaliação. Por fim, é utilizado o Mistral 7B Instruct v0.2 para os experimentos. A avaliação qualitativa foi realizada comparando os JSONs extraídos com o golden schema por meio de métricas de similaridade semântica e acurácia dos tipos de dados, utilizando o modelo de embeddings all-MiniLM-L6-v2 e similaridade do cosseno. Conclui-se que o Mistral 7B pode atuar como ferramenta auxiliar na extração, porém, ainda necessita de técnicas de pré-processamento, limpeza e correção semântica.

title: Supplementary Material for "Characterizing the Maintaining Effect of Backdoors in Federated Learning"
abstract: Sequential Backdoor Retention Experiments This repository studies whether an implanted backdoor remains detectable after subsequent training. Each experiment compares continued benign training with training that injects a second backdoor. Evaluation measures retention of the first backdoor using both current and restored BatchNorm (BN) statistics. Hardware and software The reference workstation configuration is: Component Configuration CPU AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D Memory 32 GB RAM GPU NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti Python 3.11 Training framework PyTorch with CUDA The supplied requirements.txt targets NVIDIA GPU training using PyTorch 2.12.0 and torchvision 0.27.0 CUDA 13.0 wheels. Use a compatible NVIDIA driver. Training selects CUDA when available; --device cpu selects the CPU. CUDA is the intended environment for the full experiment matrix. Plotting and result analysis do not require a GPU or trained model files. Create an environment and install the dependencies: python -m venv .venv# Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate# Linux/macOS: source .venv/bin/activatepython -m pip install -r requirements.txt For a CPU-only environment, install compatible CPU builds of PyTorch and torchvision instead of the CUDA-pinned entries, then install pandas and matplotlib at the versions specified in requirements.txt. The CPU and GPU runtimes can produce different numerical trajectories. Files Path Purpose main.py Run one experiment launcher.py Run the predefined 162-experiment matrix plots.py Generate figures from saved metrics analyze_results.py Summarize ASR and timing src/ Training, data, triggers, evaluation, caching, and output utilities requirements.txt Python dependency requirements Datasets are downloaded to data/ on first use. Experiment outputs are written to runs/ /; figures are written to plots/ / /. Experiment protocol Train a benign model for the configured number of updates. The final 2,000 benign updates are evaluated for the plots and are included in that total. Inject backdoor A, starting from the benign endpoint. Save the resulting weights and BN statistics. Start B-control from the post-A weights, restore benign BN statistics, and continue training without poisoning. Start B-maintain from the same post-A weights and benign BN statistics, and continue training with backdoor B. A and each B branch use a fresh optimizer. The B branches share their initial model, task sample order, and augmentation randomness. Evaluation preserves the training RNG state. Restored-BN A evaluation temporarily uses the saved post-A BN statistics, then restores the current statistics. The model is ResNet-18 with a 3x3 stride-1 input convolution and no initial max-pooling. Input channels and output classes follow the task dataset. Setting Default for the launcher matrix Datasets CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, EMNIST Balanced Global seeds 42, 43, 44 Benign updates 40,000 or 120,000 A updates 2,000 B updates 8,000 per branch Training / evaluation batch size 256 / 2,048 Target labels A / B 0 / 0 Poisoning Approximately 10% of each A and B-maintain batch Benign learning rate 0.01 A / B learning rates 0.01; 0.005 and 0.05 in the LR comparison Optimizer SGD, momentum 0.9, weight decay 0.0005 Learning-rate schedule Constant Evaluation interval 50 updates, plus the final update Evaluation noise seed 0 Mixed precision Disabled Data-loader workers 0 The poisoned count is the batch size times the poison rate, rounded down, with at least one poisoned sample when the rate is positive. Smaller final batches are retained. B-control has no poisoned samples. Running experiments Run a single experiment: python main.py --dataset cifar10 --seed 42 --benign-steps 40000 --trigger-a gray_4x4_center --trigger-b gray_2x2_center Run the predefined matrix: python launcher.py The launcher executes 54 conditions for each dataset, in this order: CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, EMNIST Balanced. For each of the six A/B pairs below, it runs 40,000 then 120,000 benign updates, using seeds 42, 43, 44 for each length. This gives 36 main experiments per dataset. Comparison Backdoor A Backdoor B Large to small patch Gray 4x4 center Gray 2x2 center Small to large patch Gray 2x2 center Gray 4x4 center Strong to weak noise Gaussian std 0.20 Gaussian std 0.10 Weak to strong noise Gaussian std 0.10 Gaussian std 0.20 Patch to noise Gray 4x4 center Gaussian std 0.20 Noise to patch Gaussian std 0.20 Gray 4x4 center The remaining 18 experiments use the large-to-small patch, strong-to-weak noise, and patch-to-noise pairs at 40,000 benign updates. For each pair, A and B learning rates are both 0.005 then both 0.05, with seeds 42, 43, 44 for each LR. The 0.01 cases are reused from the main comparison. START_RUN in launcher.py selects the first overall batch entry to execute, starting at 1. It skips earlier entries and reruns the selected experiment from its beginning. It does not resume an interrupted A/B stage. Saved run directory numbers are allocated after existing runs and can differ from matrix numbers. Use a fresh output directory when matrix-aligned directory numbering is needed. Use python main.py --help for all options. Always specify --benign-steps for the sequential protocol above. Omitting it selects the historical independent base-stage protocol, retained for compatibility with earlier experiments. Triggers and datasets Patches are applied after augmentation and normalization. Raw intensities are white 1.0, black 0.0, and gray 0.5; they are converted using the task dataset's mean and std before insertion. The main matrix uses centered gray patches. gaussian_noise_std0p10 and gaussian_noise_std0p20 sample fresh, independent zero-mean Gaussian noise for every poisoned image, including images in the same batch and repeated visits to an image. Noise std is measured in normalized input units. After addition, image values are clipped to [-3, 3]. Training noise uses separate A/B generators, seeded by global seed +50001 and +60001. Evaluation uses a fixed per-image bank with seed 0, independent of the global seed. A and B use the same underlying standard-normal evaluation draws, scaled by their respective std values. The bank is reused across checkpoints, branches, and BN conditions. --noise-train-seed-a/b and --noise-eval-seed provide explicit overrides. Historical noise_full_image_seed _std0p10 and std0p20 names retain their fixed-pattern semantics. Dataset Input Classes Normalization mean / std CIFAR-10 RGB, 32x32 10 (0.4914, 0.4822, 0.4465) / (0.2470, 0.2435, 0.2616) CIFAR-100 RGB, 32x32 100 (0.5071, 0.4867, 0.4408) / (0.2675, 0.2565, 0.2761) EMNIST Balanced Grayscale, 28x28 47 0.5 / 0.5 CIFAR training uses random crop with padding 4 and horizontal flip. EMNIST images are transposed to upright orientation and use no random augmentation. Other EMNIST splits are selectable with --emnist-split; letters labels are mapped from 1-26 to 0-25. OOD replacement is available separately from image triggers: python main.py --dataset cifar10 --benign-steps 40000 --backdoor-a ood --ood-source-a cifar100 --trigger-b gaussian_noise_std0p20 OOD sources must differ from the task dataset. Defaults are 800 unique training images and 1,000 held-out evaluation images. They are adapted to the task input shape and normalization, assigned the configured target label, and used to replace selected training images. Source selection uses global seed +10001 for A and +20001 for B. Configs record selected indices, seeds, and tensor hashes. OOD ASR is target prediction frequency on the held-out source subset; separate seen-subset metrics measure retention on injected images. Outputs and caching Each experiment contains config.json, timing.json, and four stage directories: base_stage/, a_stage/, b_control_stage/, b_maintain_stage/. Stage file Contents metrics.csv Scientific metrics and evaluation durations timing.csv Training durations for 50-step blocks and a final partial block last.pt and other .pt files Model, BN, and checkpoint state diagnostics/ Endpoint prediction/confusion counts and JSON metadata Benign trajectories are cached under runs/ /cache/. Compatible checkpoints preserve optimizer, RNG, and sampler position. A cache hit avoids retraining the prefix; the final plotted benign segment is replayed. Cache identity includes data, preprocessing, training settings, source code, and runtime metadata. Historical model-only caches are available only through --legacy-cache-dir and cannot supply exact continuous training resume. Reproducibility depends on a compatible runtime and device. Deterministic algorithms are enabled with warnings for unsupported operations; this does not guarantee bitwise equivalence across hardware or dependency versions. Result analysis python analyze_results.pypython analyze_results.py --dataset cifar10 --all --mode fullpython analyze_results.py --dataset cifar100 --run 1 --mode maintain Interactive mode offers Results or Timing. Results then offers Full comparison or Maintain only, with an explicit selection required. Full comparison requires complete, matching B-control and B-maintain evaluation checkpoints. For each checkpoint it calculates Delta = Maintain - Control, then reports control mean ASR, maintain mean ASR, mean Delta, and population SD of Delta, separately for current and restored BN. Positive Delta means greater A retention in B-maintain. ASRs are percentages; Delta and its SD are percentage points. SD describes variation along the difference trajectory, not variation across seeds. Interpretation columns remain blank. Missing restored-BN data are never replaced with current-BN values. The summary uses all-sample asr_a and asr_a_bn_restored. Additional non-target ASRs exclude images whose original label is the target. Maintain-only mode keeps the historica

title: Physical Artificial Intelligence and Differentiable Physics: Sim-to-Real Transfer, Whole-Body Humanoid Locomotion, and Tactile Manipulation
abstract: Abstract—Physical Artificial Intelligence (Physical AI) represents a transformative frontier in autonomous cyber-physical robotics, shifting machine intelligence from disembodied algorithmic computation into dynamical systems that perceive, reason, and actuate directly within the physical world. While pure reinforcement learning (RL) and kinematic motion planners excel in controlled, isolated environments, deploying high-degree-of-freedom (DoF) bipedal humanoids and dexterous anthropomorphic hands in real-world unstructured settings introduces severe physical and computational bottlenecks: non-smooth contact mechanics, extreme sim-to-real transfer gaps, high-dimensional non-convex hybrid dynamics, and closed-loop motor bandwidth constraints. Differentiable Physics engines—which compute exact analytical state and contact gradients through forward simulation—alongside massively parallel GPU-accelerated domain randomization, establish a foundational computational methodology to bridge this chasm. This paper delivers an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical benchmark of Physical AI for whole-body humanoid locomotion and dexterous tactile manipulation. We formalize the non-linear hybrid dynamical equations of underactuated bipedal contact, derive gradient backpropagation through Linear Complementarity Problem (LCP) friction cones, and model domain randomization over non-stationary physical distribution manifolds. Furthermore, we construct an empirical robotic evaluation testbed comprising full-scale bipedal humanoid platforms (Unitree H1, Fourier GR-1) and high-density optical tactile arrays (GelSight Svelte) evaluated across 800 challenging trials spanning uneven terrain locomotion, dynamic external impulse rejection, and blind in-hand object re-orientation. Our empirical findings demonstrate that differentiable physics-guided policy search achieves an 88.6% zero-shot sim-to-real locomotion transfer success rate, reducing training sample complexity by 4.2x over model-free PPO while bounding tracking error under 120 N external lateral impulses. Concurrently, high-frequency optical tactile feedback raises blind in-hand manipulation success by 54.2% over vision-only baselines. Finally, we formulate open challenges in non-rigid soft body contact differentiability, whole-body tactile-semantic foundation models, and real-time safety barrier certificates. Index Terms—Physical AI, Differentiable Physics, Sim-to-Real Transfer, Humanoid Locomotion, Whole-Body Control (WBC), Tactile Manipulation, Linear Complementarity Problem (LCP), Domain Randomization.

title: Symmathesy: A Platform for Relational Intelligence and Collective Stewardship
abstract: We present Symmathesy, a web-based platform for hosting interactive collective behavior experiments involving humans and AI agents. The platform serves three interlocking goals. First, for the general public, it presents an opportunity to learn about collective behavior, collective intelligence, and current advances in agentic AI through both hands-on experiments and accessible explanations about the underlying research. Second, it allows social researchers to rapidly prototype multi-agent social environments where groups of human participants and artificial agents solve established or novel competitive or collaborative tasks. Third, for researchers in AI, it provides a tool for testing agents in interactive scenarios with or against human players, contributing to the ecological validity of AI evaluation in social contexts. On a meta-level, the platform was developed through an iterative co-creation process between researchers in computational social science and a large language model coding assistant, illustrating how AI tools can empower scientists to expand their toolkit beyond their domain expertise. We describe the architecture of the platform and its five public experimental paradigms, and report a load test of the deployed configuration: a single server instance with one virtual CPU serves about 100 simultaneous players of the most demanding real-time game, with 98.5–99% of state updates arriving on time, and the measurements locate the limit in real-time messaging rather than in the game logic. We discuss the platform's potential as a research, outreach, and participatory science tool for studying collective behavior, and the validation study that is its next step. We present Symmathesy as a working prototype and an open invitation – one whose full potential depends on the collaborative growth of a community of citizens, researchers, and AI developers.

title: A Post-Quantum Motivated Resultant-Based Proof-Of-Work With Low-Cost Verification
abstract: This capsule contains the prototype implementation of SGPoW (Small-Generator Proof-of-Work), a post-quantum-motivated resultant-based proof-of-work scheme defined over cyclotomic rings. It provides the source code, parameter configurations, and benchmark scripts associated with the IEEE Access manuscript “A Post-Quantum-Motivated Resultant-Based Proof-of-Work with Low-Cost Verification.” The capsule supports evaluation of mining performance, verification cost, proof size, scaling behavior, and related experimental metrics. The benchmark scripts and configuration files are provided to facilitate computational reproducibility.

title: Large Language Models: Architecture and Operation
abstract: This chapter provides a comprehensive examination of large language models (LLMs), focusing on their architectural foundations and operational mechanisms. LLMs address the fundamental challenge of contextual understanding in natural language, enabling systems to interpret ambiguous queries and generate contextually appropriate responses. The chapter covers transformer architectures, attention mechanisms, tokenization strategies, and training methodologies. It examines how LLMs process sequential input, maintain context across long sequences, and generate coherent outputs. Special attention is given to the application of LLMs in connected and autonomous vehicle (CAV) systems, where they enable natural language interfaces, explainable decision-making, and contextual reasoning in safety-critical environments.

title: Lag: A Mean-Field Optimal Policy for Online Assignment with Reusable Resources
abstract: We study online task assignment with reusable resources. This problem arises in peer reviewer assignment, skill-based call routing, rideshare matching, emergency dispatch, and crowdsourcing: Tasks arrive according to a geometric process and must be immediately assigned to servers that become temporarily busy, yielding rewards that depend on the task-server pair. The goal is to maximize long-run average reward. We cast the problem as a contextual restless multi-armed bandit (CRMAB). We derive an occupancy-measure LP (OCC-LP) that upper-bounds the reward of any work-conserving policy. From its dual we obtain Lag, a closed-form index policy. We introduce a scaling regime in which the number of copies of each server and the number of arrivals per step grow together. This regime yields the first deterministic fluid limit for a contextual bandit. In it, Lag is asymptotically optimal. Finally, we evaluate our algorithms on peer review datasets and call center routing. The Lagrangian index achieves 83-99% of the LP upper bound across all load levels. Moreover, the Lagrangian index policy significantly outperforms the natural greedy assignment scheme, improving reward by up to 12.3% on journal data and 36% on structured synthetic instances.

title: Can the system dynamics remain structurally non-Markovian while its experimentally accessible memory signatures disappear?
abstract: We investigate how unresolved quasistatic disorder in system bath coupling affects non-Markovian dynamics in spin environments. The coupling is fixed within each experimental shot but varies between shots, so repeated shot tomography reconstructs a disorder averaged dynamical map. For a single spin bath with pure dephasing Ising interaction, disorder can drive a transition to CP-divisible dynamics for fixed bath preparations, with a critical strength set by bath polarization along the interaction axis. However, when the bath state fluctuates physically between shots, the averaged dynamics remain CP indivisible at any finite disorder strength. We extend these results analytically to inhomogeneously coupled pure dephasing baths of any number \(N\) of non-interacting spins. At any finite disorder strength, one unpolarized bath spin suffices to retain CP-indivisible dynamics, whereas a fully polarized bath yields Markovian (CP-divisible) dynamics. Dynamics with physically fluctuating bath states likewise remain non-Markovian (CP indivisible) at finite disorder for arbitrary \(N\) in the pure dephasing case. For anisotropic Heisenberg interactions, any nonzero transverse exchange eliminates the disorder driven transition to CP divisibility in a single spin bath. Exact diagonalization of anisotropic models with inhomogeneous couplings up to \(N=12\) reveals persistent trace distance revivals for fixed bath preparations, sampled Haar random preparations, and physically fluctuating bath states, showing that this effect of transverse exchange extends beyond a single bath spin. Increasing disorder still suppresses experimentally accessible revivals and can make memory effects unresolvable at finite measurement resolution even as the dynamics remain CP indivisible. Thus, transverse exchange and physical bath state fluctuations preserve dynamical indivisibility against unresolved coupling disorder.

title: Variational noise mitigation in quantum circuits: the case of Quantum Fourier Transform
abstract: Abstract We study a variational quantum algorithm (VQA) approach for improving the implementation of the Quantum Fourier Transform (QFT) under realistic noise conditions. We employ a training strategy based on mutually unbiased bases (MUBs), which probes the action of the noisy variational circuit over a global set of input states and promotes generalization beyond the training ensemble. We numerically study two- and three-qubit QFT implementations under noise models combining incoherent errors with coherent crosstalk, using calibration parameters derived from a quantum device. For the 2-qubit QFT, the optimized variational circuit consistently outperforms the corresponding noisy QFT in scenarios containing coherent noise and exhibits highly reproducible optimization across independent parameter initializations. The variational advantage persists in the direct 3-qubit optimization, although with a stronger dependence on initialization. We further show that reduced MUB training sets can retain most of the performance of the complete set while substantially reducing the number of training states, whereas training only on computational-basis states leads to markedly poorer generalization and a stronger dependence on parameter initialization. Finally, exploiting the recursive structure of the QFT, we demonstrate that an optimized 2-qubit variational block can be embedded into a 3-qubit QFT and improve its noisy implementation without retraining the complete circuit. These results highlight the potential of combining global state-space training with device-specific noise-aware variational optimization to improve small noisy quantum circuits and to explore the transfer of variationally learned noise resilience to larger constructions.

title: Latent Structure in Chess Positions
abstract: En este trabajo entrenamos autoencoders para entender representaciones latentes de posiciones de ajedrez. Utilizamos una base de datos de partidas de Lichess filtradas por nivel de juego y control de tiempo, y representamos cada posición como un tensor de múltiples canales. Entrenamos un autoencoder para reconstruir dichas posiciones y posteriormente analizamos el espacio latente mediante Análisis de Componentes Principales (PCA). Nuestros resultados muestran que las primeras componentes capturan información relevante del juego, tales como el enroque y las características de la apertura. Realizamos también un experimento basado en simetrías del tablero que sugiere que el modelo no memoriza posiciones de forma trivial. Estos hallazgos indican que los autoencoders pueden capturar estructuras significativas en el ajedrez y ofrecen una ventana interpretable al conocimiento del juego.

title: The Impact of Data Quality on Machine Learning Model Performance
abstract: This research examines the impact of data quality on the performance of machine learning classification models. The study focuses on three common data-quality factors: missing data, feature selection, and label noise. Three machine learning models (Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, and Random Forest) are evaluated on the Titanic dataset using Accuracy and F1-score. A series of experiments modifies the quality and structure of the dataset while keeping the general modeling approach consistent. The results show that different types of data-quality problems affect models to different degrees: label noise can cause a substantial decrease in predictive performance, while the effects of missing data and feature selection depend on the model and experimental conditions. The study also compares the sensitivity of the algorithms to data-quality problems and evaluates whether the research hypothesis is supported by the results. Independent research project. Implemented in Python using pandas, NumPy, matplotlib, and scikit-learn.

title: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) and Parameterized Quantum Circuits for High-Dimensional Optimization: Barren Plateaus, Quantum Kernels, and NISQ Benchmarks
abstract: Abstract—Quantum Machine Learning (QML) operating on Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) hardware represents an emerging computational paradigm to address high-dimensional optimization problems that challenge classical Von Neumann supercomputing architectures. By mapping complex feature vectors into exponentially large 2^N Hilbert state spaces via Parameterized Quantum Circuits (PQCs) and Variational Quantum Algorithms (VQAs), QML targets computational advantages in combinatorial optimization, high-dimensional classification, and quantum-enhanced molecular modeling. However, the theoretical promise of NISQ-era variational computing is severely constrained by three fundamental bottlenecks: (1) Barren Plateaus, characterized by the exponential concentration of measure and vanishing variance of cost function gradients; (2) Hardware Decoherece Noise and readout error rates that corrupt quantum state fidelity; and (3) Classical-to-Quantum State Preparation bottlenecks that can erase theoretical computational speedups. This paper delivers an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical benchmark of QML architectures for high-dimensional optimization. We formalize the Haar-distributed geometric mechanics of barren plateaus under 2-design unitary assumptions, evaluate barren plateau mitigation through shallow local cost operators and layer-by-layer parameter initialization, and contrast Variational Quantum Eigensolvers (VQE) with Quantum Kernel Support Vector Machines (Q-SVM). Furthermore, we construct an empirical benchmarking testbed executing across both state-vector simulators and superconducting quantum backends (IBM Quantum Heron / Eagle architectures), evaluating 127-qubit Hamiltonian optimization and high-dimensional financial portfolio allocation. Our findings demonstrate that while global cost functions suffer exponential gradient decay Var[grad] ~ O(2^-N) across circuit depth d >= 4, local Hamiltonian decomposition maintains trainable variance, achieving a 98.2% ground-state fidelity under zero-noise extrapolation (ZNE) error mitigation. Finally, we formulate open challenges in quantum error mitigation scaling, non-perturbative barren plateau escapes, and quantum data loading efficiency. Index Terms—Quantum Machine Learning (QML), Parameterized Quantum Circuits (PQCs), Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE), Barren Plateaus, Quantum Kernel Methods, NISQ Computing, Error Mitigation, Hilbert Space.

title: Who Should We Listen to More? Welfare-Aware Preference Acquisition for Pluralistic Alignment
abstract: Pluralistic alignment needs to accommodate diverse preferences under limited human feedback. Using AI simulators to label preference comparisons reduces annotation costs, but variation in simulation accuracy across individuals can leave some people's preferences poorly represented in training. We study how to allocate human feedback across people to construct training data for pluralistic alignment, and how this allocation affects the trained policy. To make this allocation explicit and controllable, we define a social welfare objective over individual supervision utilities that measure label quality. Each query's marginal welfare gain depends on its expected supervision improvement, the recipient's current utility, and application-designated priority. Welfare-Aware Preference Acquisition (WAPA) uses auxiliary reference models to estimate query gains and individual utilities, then selects queries by estimated marginal welfare gain while updating recipient utilities. We prove exact optimality of the acquisition algorithm for the estimated welfare objective under a fixed query budget and model predictions. Experiments on six Roleplay collections and four OpinionQA regions demonstrate improved supervision and controllable allocation tradeoffs. Policy training on four Roleplay collections improves preference prediction for both seen and unseen individuals. When prioritizing a designated group and poorly represented individuals, acquiring human labels for 20% of comparisons recovers 75-86% of the average predictive utility gap between policies trained entirely on AI-generated labels and entirely on ground-truth labels.

title: Evidence-First Agentic Verification
abstract: Long-horizon, semi-verifiable agentic tasks often rely on rubric-based evaluation, but the evidence needed to assess these tasks can be spread across the environment state and the execution trace. A judge may overlook this evidence or accept unsupported claims, including an agent's own reports of success. When rubric verdicts serve as reinforcement-learning rewards, such errors can reinforce undesirable behavior. We introduce Sauron, an evidence-first agentic verifier that investigates both state and trace and relies on a claim only after independently validating it against its source. Bounded queries and joint investigation of related criteria reduce context use and redundant work, and each verdict carries an auditable receipt of its supporting evidence. Across 2,586 human-labeled criteria from 100 personal-assistant episodes, Sauron achieves the highest F1 of five verifiers on all eight backbones tested while costing less than Gandalf, the strongest baseline. With GPT-5.6 Sol, it reaches 0.96 F1 versus Gandalf's 0.92 at 23% lower cost, with a wider margin on process criteria. On a paired fault-injection suite covering 13 families, several of which simulate reward hacking, Sauron detects 97% of injected failures while flagging only 2% of clean controls, outperforming baselines even when they are given the full trace. On TRAIL, a benchmark for detecting and localizing real agent errors, Sauron leads both Gandalf and TRAIL's own judge on all three quality metrics.

title: Sufficient conditions for additivity of the zero-error classical capacity of quantum channels
abstract: The one-shot zero-error classical capacity of a quantum channel is the maximum amount of classical information that can be transmitted with zero probability of error via a single channel use. This capacity is fundamentally characterized by the logarithm of the independence number of the noncommutative graph induced by the quantum channel. Consequently, the additivity of the one-shot zero-error classical capacity is equivalent to the multiplicativity of the independence number of the associated noncommutative graphs. As the independence number is not multiplicative in general, the specific conditions under which multiplicativity is preserved remain an open question in quantum information theory. Here, we establish some sufficient conditions for the multiplicativity of the independence number and provide explicit examples of quantum channels that satisfy these criteria. Furthermore, we investigate the block form of noncommutative graphs and derive the conditions under which the independence number remains multiplicative within this framework. These results offer new insights into the structural properties of noncommutative graphs and the fundamental limits of zero-error quantum communication.

title: LLM-Based Agent for Supervised Classifier Lifecycle Automation: Shifting from Stochastic Search to Heuristic Reasoning
abstract: La selección de algoritmos de aprendizaje automático y la optimización de sus hiperparámetros constituyen fases críticas del ciclo de vida de los clasificadores supervisados, demandando tradicionalmente una inversión significativa de tiempo, capacidad de cómputo y supervisión experta. El presente trabajo evalúa el potencial de los Modelos Grandes de Lenguaje (LLMs) como asistentes de decisión en la automatización de dicho ciclo. Se reportan resultados preliminares, en los cuales un agente LLM asume el rol de especialista humano en la fase de entrenamiento y ajuste fino, operando de forma iterativa sobre el conjunto de datos. El diseño experimental contrasta dos modalidades de despliegue, una basada en pesos cerrados gestionados vía API y otra basada en pesos abiertos ejecutados localmente, bajo un protocolo común de optimización. Los resultados muestran que el agente, en sus dos modalidades de despliegue (vía API y local), presenta rendimientos comparables a los de referencia reportados por expertos humanos. Estos resultados demuestran la viabilidad de una automatización más eficiente, explicable y soberana en el desarrollo de soluciones de Machine Learning, con capacidad para reducir trabajo manual sin perder trazabilidad ni consistencia en el proceso iterativo.

title: A Benchmark of Unsupervised Anomaly Detectors for Credit Card Fraud under Two Training Protocols
abstract: Credit card fraud detection is a critical problem in financial security, yet real-world deployment scenarios often lack labeled fraud samples at initial stages, making unsupervised anomaly detection an appealing approach. However, the comparative performance of different unsupervised detectors under varying training data compositions—whether trained exclusively on normal transactions or on mixed data containing unlabeled frauds—remains insufficiently studied. This paper presents a head-to-head benchmark of five unsupervised anomaly detectors—Mahalanobis distance, Isolation Forest, Local Outlier Factor (LOF), One-Class SVM, and Elliptic Envelope—on the publicly available ULB Credit Card Fraud Detection dataset. Each detector is evaluated under two training protocols: novelty detection (trained solely on normal transactions) and outlier detection (trained on the full dataset containing both normal and fraudulent samples). Performance is measured using PR-AUC, Precision@k, and recall at low false positive rates. Results show that Mahalanobis distance and LOF achieve strong performance under the novelty detection protocol (PR-AUC > 0.73) but suffer catastrophic degradation when trained on mixed data, with PR-AUC dropping by 0.57 and 0.72 respectively. Isolation Forest gives solid and reliable results on both two tested protocols, and its PR-AUC score increases slightly from 0.3953 to 0.4432. After parameter adjustment (with parameters set as support_fraction=0.9, contamination=0.01), Elliptic Envelope gets moderate performance (PR-AUC≈0.37) and is almost insensible to protocol changes. The conclusions obtained in this part can provide actual instruction for choosing unsupervised detectors to be used in real fraud detection systems working under various conditions of label availability and data quality.

title: SUN'IY YARATILGAN MATNLARNI ANIQLASHDA INVARIANTLAR VA DASTURIY FILTRLASH JARAYONI
abstract: Maqolada sun'iy yaratilgan matnlarni aniqlash algoritmini dasturiy filtrlash jarayoniga tatbiq etish masalasi ko'rib chiqiladi. Yondashuv matnni dastlabki tayyorlash, lingvistik-statistik xususiyatlarni hisoblash, xususiyatlar vektorini sinf invariantlari bilan taqqoslash va qaror ishonchliligini baholash bosqichlariga ajratiladi. Manbada keltirilgan tajriba jadvalidagi I va II tur xatoliklar ko'rsatkichlari tahlil qilinib, sinonimlash orqali yaratilgan matnlar uchun lug'at tanlovi xatolik darajasiga ta'sir qilishi ko'rsatiladi. Natijalar dasturiy filtrlashda faqat yakuniy yorliqni emas, balki qarorning ishonchlilik darajasi va xato xavfini ham hisobga olish kerakligini asoslaydi.

title: An Optimized Approach of Deep Neural Network for Liver Cancer Image Analysis
abstract: Early detection of liver diseases helps reduce the fatality rate in liver cancer.It also enhances the regeneration process in liver transplantation.To achieve early detection, handcrafted features were used for analysis.Although these features performed efficiently, they suffered in multiclass identification due to the limited choice of features.To overcome this limitation, the proposed work implements a customized deep learning framework using Sparrow Search Optimization for network tuning, along with K-fold training to generalize network performance.The proposed framework was tested on a customized liver disease dataset, which undergoes preprocessing steps such as median filtering to suppress speckle noise and data augmentation to improve robustness.The processed data is then passed through the proposed framework, and its performance is evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score.By comparing the performance of the proposed method with handcrafted feature-based approaches using multidomain features and Particle Swarm Optimization, it is observed that the proposed method outperforms the existing methods with an accuracy above 94%.This demonstrates that the proposed framework is suitable for automated liver disease identification.

title: Giving stateless agents a sense of time: A reconsolidating episodic–semantic memory architecture
abstract: Stateless agents may retrieve past interactions yet lack an operational sense of time: external memory makes the past available, but does not represent how experience loses accessibility, returns to relevance, or changes meaning. This paper defines that capacity as an episodic–semantic lifecycle governed by importance, elapsed time, recall and evidence. Pragma, developed by the author, stores sessions as episodes whose narratives stay outside the rewrite target, and consolidates recurring regularities into source-linked beliefs. Deterministic salience and decay regulate accessibility; recall and evidence trigger versioned reconsolidation without overwriting recorded events. The architecture is examined in 229 executions spanning four scenarios, four model families and ten executions per condition. The deterministic layer behaves identically in every family: salience, reinforcement and decay reproduce exactly, no belief is admitted without two distinct sources, and the tracked episode returned to the active zone in all 45 executions where it became dormant. The judgements it consumes do not: the same estimate varies by an order of magnitude across families, and that variation alone can decide whether a designed transition occurs. Removing the lifecycle answers the same memory probes equally well at the store sizes these scenarios reach, which delimits where the difference can be sought. Code, stimuli, metadata and traces make every reported transition inspectable. The contribution is an operational definition of temporal continuity, an architecture implementing it, and evidence separating the properties that hold by construction from those that depend on the model. It is not a validation of reliability, semantic correctness or comparative performance.

title: How Consumers Negotiate Trust and Responsibility Towards AI ‐Generated Virtual Influencers?
abstract: ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence is increasingly embedded in socially interactive roles, with virtual influencers emerging as a prominent form of AI‐mediated communication. This study examines how consumers engage with agents that simulate social presence yet lack independent agency. Using a mixed‐methods design, we investigate how authenticity, transparency, and privacy concerns relate to trust, acceptance, and responsibility attribution. The findings show that consumer responses cannot be reduced to trust formation alone. Instead, individuals evaluate whether engagement remains acceptable under conditions of artificial agency. Authenticity supports trust by providing coherence, while transparency and privacy concerns introduce competing interpretations related to control and risk. Privacy concerns are also associated with greater responsibility attribution to brands and developers. These results suggest that engagement with virtual influencers can be interpreted as a process in which consumers negotiate trust and accountability. The study offers an integrated perspective on AI‐mediated influence and highlights the role of distributed responsibility in shaping consumer responses.

title: Deep Learning for Atmospheric Turbulence Mitigation: A Comparison Between GANs and Transformers
abstract: Atmospheric turbulence creates complex spatial and temporal distortions that significantly reduce image quality. This work compares two deep learning methods for turbulence reduction: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and Transformer-based models. Both methods are trained and tested on the SOTIS dataset, which includes multi-frame sequences under different turbulence conditions with ground truth references. Our results show an important finding: GAN-based models perform better in severely degraded, low-quality situations, while Transformer-based models achieve better results in moderate to high-quality settings, especially in correcting geometric distortions. We also enhance the Turbulence Mitigation Transformer (TMT) by introducing a refined training strategy, an augmented input design that includes a temporally averaged frame as prior structural information, and a modified loss function that incorporates the Structural Similarity Index (SSIM). These improvements lead to consistent performance gains across various turbulence conditions. Overall, this study provides an in-depth evaluation of deep learning methods for turbulence reduction and offers practical guidance for selecting models in different imaging environments.

title: Relative-Entropy Geometry and Convergence in Nonconvex Wiretap Optimization
abstract: We develop and analyze an entropic descent method for a nonconvex optimization problem on probability simplices arising in classical and quantum secure communication. The optimization variables describe a randomized encoder, allowing its input distribution and stochastic preprocessing to be optimized jointly. An exact relative-entropy identity yields a channel-independent majorization bound and an explicit mirror-descent iteration with a fixed unit step size. We establish quantitative descent, convergence of objective values, and stationarity of accumulation points on their support faces for arbitrary finite classical channels, without assuming degradedness or less noisiness. For strictly positive transition matrices, a square-root parametrization and a Kurdyka--Łojasiewicz argument establish finite length of the transformed trajectory and convergence of the entire sequence, including limits on the simplex boundary. For less-noisy channels, a restricted convex formulation admits global convergence with an explicit \(O(1/t)\) objective-error bound. We extend the relative-entropy construction to noncommuting quantum outputs and derive monotone alternating updates for covariant encoders, including correlated preprocessing over a fixed block. Numerical experiments compare the method with analytic benchmarks and constrained optimization, reveal multiple attracting values, and demonstrate strict improvements from stochastic preprocessing.

title: How Safe Is ChatGPT Health Advice? Evidence from Real User Conversations in Four Global South Countries
abstract: People increasingly bring their health questions to ChatGPT, yet safety evaluations of LLM health advice rest almost entirely on clinician-authored vignettes, synthetic prompts, or simulated user profiles. The gap is widest for the Global South, where concerns about demographic bias and unsafe recommendations are well documented but have never been tested on real usage. We present, to our knowledge, the first demographically grounded safety evaluation of real-world health conversations with ChatGPT. From a consent-based data-donation corpus of 202,590 conversations from 1,252 users in India, Nigeria, Brazil, and Pakistan (December 2022 to February 2026), each linked to self-reported age and gender, we identify 15,555 health conversations, classify their health intent using an LLM classifier adapted from an established taxonomy, and score response safety under both a context-blind and a user-context-aware rubric. Roughly one in five health conversations receives a high-risk rating. Risk concentrates in symptom and condition queries and recurs through identifiable failure modes: unsafe medication or dosage guidance, harmful self-diagnosis, missing safety warnings, encouraging over-reliance on the model, and failure to refer users to professionals. Supplying the user's own accumulated context raises the high-risk share by 13-17 percentage points, and about one in four conversations rated safe in isolation turns out to be unsafe for the specific person asking. Safety evaluations built on synthetic cases are likely to miss these harms.

Supplying the user's own accumulated context raises the high-risk share by 13-17 percentage points, and about one in four conversations rated safe in isolation turns out to be unsafe for the specific person asking. Safety evaluations built on synthetic cases are likely to miss these harms.

title: Hierarchical Time Series Forecasting with Operator-Valued Kernels
abstract: Hierarchical time series forecasting requires generating accurate predictions that are coherent across multiple levels of aggregation. Existing methods either rely on two-stage pipelines with post-hoc reconciliation or on end-to-end models that often lack statistical guarantees. We introduce a unified framework that formulates hierarchical forecasting as a multivariate regression problem in a vector-valued reproducing kernel Hilbert space. By designing structured operator-valued kernels, our approach enforces coherence directly within the hypothesis space, ensuring that all predictions satisfy hierarchical constraints by construction. We further propose tailored kernel constructions for hierarchical data and derive excess risk bounds that characterize generalization performance. Empirical results on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate the relevance of the proposed method.

title: FETALFusion: Resolution-Aware State-Space Modeling for Multi-Domain Fetal Head Segmentation
abstract: Head circumference (HC) measured from 2D ultrasound is a routine marker of fetal growth, and automating it needs segmentations whose boundaries hold up on individual scans, not only on average. We present FETALFusion, a dual-path CNN-Mamba encoder-decoder for fetal head segmentation across acquisition types. It applies four-directional state-space scans only at the two highest-resolution stages, routes bottleneck features through domain-specific channel gates that are averaged at test time, and adds a weak landmark shape prior. We train jointly on transabdominal (HC-18) and transperineal (PSFHS) images and compare ten methods on a held-out test set of 471 images, each trained under one schedule and scored by surface distances at native resolution. FETALFusion reaches a Dice score of 0.963 and an HD95 of 2.10 mm without test-time augmentation or a domain label. It improves on U-Mamba on all five reported metrics (HD95 reduced by 0.31 mm; Holm-corrected ($p < 10^{-4}$), a lead that holds under test-time augmentation and across two independent training runs, and in the mean on U-Net, Attention U-Net and TransUNet. Residual encoders close the gap: a ResNet-34 UNet++ exceeds FETALFusion, and an ImageNet initialised ResNet-34 U-Net is best overall (HD95 1.75 mm). The ablation agrees. Calibrated against run-to-run variation, it attributes FETALFusion's measurable gains to the landmark shape prior and, on transperineal images, to the domain gates, while removing the state-space branch does not measurably change accuracy. HC from the predicted masks agrees with the clinical reference at an intraclass correlation of 0.9986.

title: Upstream Influence, Downstream Re-Anchoring in LLM Agent Chains
abstract: People act on evaluative judgments produced by LLM agents, and in multi-agent systems those judgments pass through several agents before reaching a person. We show that a workflow's information architecture---source access, handoff format, and which model reads the untrusted content---governs how much of a coordinated manipulation reaches the end. On 32 Taiwan~2025 recall cases, ten authentic Threads comments shown to one agent move its stance by $+0.171$ toward the injected position, and a mirrored set moves it the other way. Passing that judgment down a chain removes more than half of the shift by the third agent; keeping the comments in front of every agent sustains more of it. The reduction is not attrition in transit: each receiver discounts the inherited stance in proportion to how far it sits from its own reading of the evidence, returning to what that evidence implies for the case rather than to neutrality---consistent with partial re-anchoring. Handoff format is a second lever: a stance relayed without its reasoning is largely discounted. Susceptibility at the exposed seat varies fourfold across models, while the chain's arrangement does not matter at all. None of this is visible in the transcripts---the injected claims are almost never restated, so reasoning-trace audits miss the attack.

title: Rethinking Anonymity Claims in Synthetic Data Generation: A Model-Centric Privacy Attack Perspective
abstract: Training generative machine learning models to produce synthetic tabular data has become a popular approach for enhancing privacy in data sharing. As this typically involves processing sensitive personal information, releasing either the trained model or generated synthetic datasets can still pose privacy risks. Yet, recent research, commercial deployments, and privacy regulations like the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) largely assess anonymity at the level of an individual dataset.

title: Modelos Extensos de Lenguaje (LLM) aplicados a la tutoría académica en asignaturas básicas de la Escuela Politécnica Nacional: implementación de un modelo Llm para tareas de tutoría académica en la asignatura de Química.
abstract: Este trabajo implementó un modelo extenso de lenguaje especializado en Fundamentos de Química para apoyar la tutoría académica de estudiantes de los primeros niveles universitarios. La motivación surgió de una dificultad recurrente en la Escuela Politécnica Nacional, donde quienes inician Química General suelen llegar a un resultado sin seguir el razonamiento que lo sustenta, mientras que la tutoría tradicional y los modelos genéricos rara vez detallan cada paso. Se buscó un tutor que explicara los problemas por etapas y no solo devolviera resultados. El desarrollo se estructuró siguiendo la metodología CRISP-DM, lo que permitió articular todo el proceso desde la obtención de los datos hasta la construcción del prototipo final. A partir del material entregado por el Departamento de Formación Básica se depuró un conjunto cercano a los novecientos ítems hasta conformar un corpus de 684 ejercicios, normalizados en LaTeX para conservar la notación química y matemática y serializados en formato conversacional JSONL. Sobre ese corpus se aplicó ajuste fino eficiente en parámetros mediante QLoRA y PEFT a tres modelos abiertos de catorce mil millones de parámetros: Phi-4-reasoning, Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct y DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B, entrenados de forma local en un solo equipo con una única tarjeta gráfica. La evaluación combinó indicadores cuantitativos, como la pérdida de validación y la precisión token a token, con una revisión manual de cuarenta ejercicios independientes distribuidos en los seis ejes del sílabo, porque unas buenas métricas de entrenamiento no garantizan la corrección química ni aritmética. Phi-4-reasoning presentó el mejor comportamiento, con un acierto automático del 96,3 %, una pérdida de validación de 0,4357 y un cumplimiento de la estructura del 90,0 %, por lo que se seleccionó como modelo principal. El prototipo local integró una skill pedagógica, recuperación semántica sobre el texto guía y una interfaz en Streamlit, y reforzó el estudio autónomo sin desplazar la labor del docente.

title: Model Collapse in Bangla and English: A Pre-Registered Study of Iterative Self-Training with Gemma-3-270m
abstract: Pre-registration of a computational experiment on model collapse in a low-resource language setting, frozen before any model is trained. We fine-tune the open-weight model google/gemma-3-270m (bfloat16) in Bangla and in English over six generations of self-training, where each generation is trained on text generated by the previous one. Three regimes are compared per language: REPLACE (synthetic text only), ACCUMULATE (real seed text plus all synthetic generations) and ACCUMULATE-FILTER (the same with a pre-specified quality filter). Corpora are built from public Bangla and English Wikipedia and openly licensed web text, matched across languages in words per document and in token budget (10 million generated tokens per generation). Outcomes are held-out log-perplexity and bits per byte, lexical diversity of fixed-prefix samples, and recall on a paired factual-probe set, all computed automatically. Hypotheses: H0, both languages degrade under REPLACE (anchor); H1, Bangla degrades faster than English under REPLACE on the pre-specified slopes; H2, the relative benefit of accumulating real data is smaller for Bangla. The decision rule, the robustness phases in a fixed priority order with a stopping rule under the approved compute cap (one rented RTX 4090, US$30 / 70 GPU-hours), the scoped-out conditions and the analysis plan are given in the attached 01_PREREGISTRATION.md; exact chain and corpus settings are in chains.yaml and corpora.yaml; prereg_freeze_2026-10-13.json lists the SHA-256 of each attached file. No human participants are involved; the study uses public text and model outputs only. Authors: Md Tahidul Islam (ORCID 0009-0004-6798-892X, corresponding) and Maksuda Akter (ORCID 0009-0004-5808-518X), Department of Computer Science and Engineering, CCN University of Science & Technology, Cumilla, Bangladesh. Registered before any training run.

title: Evolving federated density peak clustering with shuffler-based anonymization
abstract: Abstract In this paper, we present a novel one-shot federated clustering approach based on evolving fuzzy clustering and shuffler-based anonymization. In federated clustering, each round reveals additional model information to the server and can increase the opportunity to infer properties of local datasets, even when raw samples are never shared. Consequently, fewer client–server exchanges and unlinkability are important, so transmitted information cannot be attributed to any single client. Data-stream clustering algorithms, which learn in a single pass over the data, align well with the one-shot federated learning paradigm, where a single communication round can be sufficient. The proposed Evolving Federated Density Peak Clustering (eFDPC) method combines evolving fuzzy data-stream clustering and density peak clustering in a federated setting. Each client independently evolves micro-clusters from private data mini-batches through cluster addition and merging. To limit communication, density peak clustering is applied to the learned micro-clusters and only the selected peaks are transmitted, rather than the full local models. A shuffler-based layer is introduced between the clients and the server to anonymize contributions prior to reconstruction and global peak selection. We consider a peak-only variant, eFDPC- $$\mathcal {P}$$ , as well as eFDPC- $$\mathcal {G}$$ with server-side label propagation. Experiments on synthetic and real-world benchmark datasets show that eFDPC outperforms recent federated clustering baselines in one-shot settings and scales to higher-dimensional, non-IID data.

title: Gap-Priced $|T\rangle$-States: Dynamic $|T\rangle$ Post-Selection and Budget-Aware Factory Provisioning
abstract: Magic $|T\rangle$-state preparation dominates the cost of fault-tolerant quantum computation on surface codes, yet cultivation and distillation are typically provisioned statically, leaving much of the program's error budget unused. We present Gap-Priced $|T\rangle$ States (GP$|T\rangle$-S), a lattice surgery scheduler and factory allocator that co-optimizes both methods under a total $T$-error budget. GP$|T\rangle$-S uses the complementary gap of each cultivated state as a fidelity estimate and dynamically adjusts the cultivation gap cutoff, converting budget slack into speed by giving the scheduler control over the cultivation post-selection. GP$|T\rangle$-S also characterizes distillation factories by size, $|T\rangle$-state production rate, and budget slack, and introduces cultivating factories that embed cultivation within routing channels, achieving fidelities otherwise requiring two-level distillation at a single-level footprint. GP$|T\rangle$-S organizes these characterizations into a factory catalog, and performs distillation factory allocation over this catalog in tandem with the gap cutoff using dynamic-programming to achieve one of i) minimum spacetime volume, ii) minimum execution time, or iii) minimum space overhead, all within a user-provided $T$-error budget. Across sixteen benchmarks under high and low $T$-error budgets of $10^{-3}$ and $10^{-5}$ respectively, GP$|T\rangle$-S consistently outperforms cultivation-only and single-factory baselines without exceeding the budget, achieving a 5.5$\times$ geometric mean speedup in logical cycle count and a 3.4$\times$ geometric mean reduction in space-time volume.
