title: Neuro-Symbolic Graph Transformers for Hierarchical Intention Recognition from Multimodal Human Activity Sequences
abstract: Proactive human-robot collaboration requires autonomous systems to infer not only immediate actions but also the underlying hierarchical intentions governing human behavior. Current deep learning approaches predominantly focus on flat action classification, failing to capture the structural dependencies connecting kinematic motion to high-level goals. A Neuro-Symbolic Graph Transformer (NSGT) is proposed within this multimodal framework, a Human Reasoning Graph (HR-G) is integrated into the self-attention mechanism via learnable topological biases. Furthermore, the architecture is augmented with a differentiable First-Order Logic (FOL) loss, acting as a structural regularizer by which ontological consistency is enforced across four levels: atomic actions, composite activities, Low-Level Intentions, and High-Level Intentions. Evaluation is performed on the synthesized NTU-Hierarchy dataset, a four-level ontological extension of NTU RGB+D 120, wherein existing sequences were mapped into 119,383 complex hierarchical episodes (85 actions, 16 activities, 8 LLIs, 4 HLIs). To prevent circular supervision, strict isolation between label generation and FOL constraints was maintained. In the base configuration, 91.65% top-1 action accuracy is achieved by the NSGT. When the FOL loss is incorporated into the baseline, logic consistency is improved by 3.26 percentage points to 96.67%. Through the HR-G biases, a tunable trade-off between accuracy and structural coherence is established. In the primary consistency-maximizing configuration ($λ$ = 0.5), a logic consistency of 94.59% is reached and ontological contradictions are reduced by 33%, while a robust 89.90% top-1 action accuracy is retained. Finally, interpretable reasoning evidence is provided by the learned HR-G weights, wherein transition edges are strongly exploited ($β$ trans $\approx$ +2.6) without explicit supervision.

title: PUGS: Physics-Guided Uncertainty Modeling for Underwater Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting
abstract: Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) provides an efficient framework for dynamic scene reconstruction. Most existing approaches model scene dynamics with deterministic deformation fields, assuming each Gaussian follows a distinct geometric trajectory over time. This assumption breaks down underwater, where light scattering, refraction, marine snow and low visibility create substantial physical ambiguity in captured images. We present PUGS, a physics-guided uncertainty model for underwater dynamic 3DGS. PUGS learns inherent uncertainty induced by underwater image formation and leverages it as a physical signal for dynamic scene modeling. Rather than estimating a single deterministic displacement, it parameterizes each Gaussian's motion as a probability distribution with expected deformation and physical uncertainty. We adopt stochastic deformation optimization to sample Gaussian trajectories via local reparameterization, exploring multiple physically plausible solutions during training. We further propose uncertainty stochastic annealing and a dual-path self-consistency distillation objective, converting stochastic exploration to deterministic reconstruction while preserving temporal coherence. Extensive experiments on underwater dynamic datasets and physics-aware benchmarks demonstrate superior rendering quality, temporal consistency and reconstruction robustness. Our method achieves 1.16 dB PSNR gain over the strongest baseline on UVEB and 3.99 dB on DRUVA.

title: Scalable Postselection of Quantum Resources
abstract: The large overhead imposed by quantum error correction is a critical challenge to the realization of quantum computers, and motivates searching for alternative error correcting codes and fault-tolerant circuit constructions. Postselection is a powerful tool that builds large programs out of probabilistically generated sub-circuits, and has been shown to increase the threshold of quantum error correction based on fusing fixed-size resource states or concatenated codes. In this work, we present an approach to lower the overhead of quantum computing using scalable postselection, based on directly postselecting sub-circuits with a size extensive in the code distance using decoder soft information. We introduce a metric, the partial gap, that estimates what the logical gap of a resource state will be after it is consumed, and show that postselection based on the partial gap leads to scalable improvements in the logical error rate. In the specific context of implementing logical gates via teleportation through a cluster state, we demonstrate that scalable postselection provides a $4\times$ reduction in the overhead per logical gate, at the same logical error probability.

title: Sistema de estudio para ingreso a la Escuela Politécnica Nacional: módulo – Asistente de Aprendizaje con LLM Local
abstract: El presente Trabajo de Integración Curricular aborda el diseño e implementación de un asistente de aprendizaje basado en un modelo de lenguaje de gran tamaño (LLM) ejecutado en entorno local, que actúa como componente orquestador de un sistema de tutoría inteligente multi-modelo para la preparación del examen de ingreso a la Escuela Politécnica Nacional. El problema de partida es que los aspirantes enfrentan el proceso de admisión con recursos de preparación heterogéneos y retroalimentación limitada, mientras que las soluciones comerciales basadas en la nube introducen restricciones de privacidad, latencia variable y ausencia de especialización en el currículo institucional. El desarrollo siguió el Modelo de Prototipos a lo largo de cinco iteraciones. En la primera se realizó una evaluación comparativa de cinco modelos de código abierto sobre tres bloques de prueba diseñados a la medida del rol de orquestación, de la que se derivó una arquitectura dual: el modelo qwen2.5:1.5b para la clasificación de consultas y qwen2.5:14b para el análisis de desempeño y la generación de rutas de aprendizaje, ambos cuantizados en formato GGUF Q4_K_M y ejecutados mediante Ollama en un servidor CPU sin GPU. En las iteraciones siguientes se implementó una API REST con FastAPI que expone los flujos de clasificación, planificación y retroalimentación; se construyó un pipeline de recuperación aumentada por generación (RAG) sobre los documentos oficiales de admisión, con embeddings multilingües almacenados en ChromaDB; y se integró el módulo con el backend Node.js/TypeScript y los modelos especialistas numérico y verbal. Las pruebas funcionales y de integración end-to-end confirmaron que el sistema completo opera de forma coordinada, desde la consulta del estudiante hasta la persistencia de la decisión académica, con latencias síncronas tolerables en la clasificación y asíncronas aceptables en la generación de planes con contexto institucional. La evaluación de la calidad del contenido generado, estructurada según los criterios del marco RAGAS, evidenció una alta pertinencia de las rutas propuestas y permitió elevar la fidelidad al contexto recuperado mediante la descomposición de la tarea de generación en dos pasos. Los resultados validan la viabilidad de construir tutores inteligentes anclados al currículo institucional sin depender de servicios en la nube ni de hardware GPU, preservando la privacidad de los datos del estudiante dentro de la infraestructura de la institución.

title: Quantum Key Distribution over Free Space Optical Satellite Links in the 6G Era
abstract: Satellite-based free-space optical links can act as time-varying optical wireless interconnects that distribute quantum resources across space-terrestrial infrastructures, complementing the 6G vision of integrated non-terrestrial networks. Among quantum communication services, Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) is the most mature and is therefore adopted as an illustrative use case. This paper develops an attenuation-centric framework for satellite QKD based on weak-coherentpulse BB84. The considered system model links orbital geometry and optical terminal parameters to an equivalent channel transmissivity, which governs detection statistics, quantum bit error rate (QBER), and secret key generation through secrecy bounds. We derive the secret-fraction cutoff behavior with respect to channel attenuation and show how it induces time-dependent secret key rates during satellite overpasses. Numerical results using orbital data and representative parameters from the 'Micius' mission show that the minimum slant range over the onemonth observation window spans approximately 400-2400 km; approximately 34% of passes have minimum slant ranges below 900 km, and favorable passes yield secret key rates on the order of a few kbps. The proposed modeling approach provides a link-level building block for future network-level studies, where scheduling and routing of quantum-secured services can be informed by predicted key generation windows over satellite optical interconnects.

title: Selecting the 7th Smallest of 16 Elements Takes Exactly 28 Comparisons: code, certificates and Lean proofs
abstract: First release of the research artifacts accompanying: Jonathan Cremer, Selecting the 7th Smallest of 16 Elements Takes Exactly 28 Comparisons. Includes: Explicit comparison-algorithm certificates for all seven new upper bounds. An independent static verifier, execution tests, and an exact path oracle. Lean 4 proofs of all seven numerical upper bounds. A separate Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization of the analytical lower-bound theory. Search code and scripts for the evaluations reported in the paper. The published numerical lower bounds used to establish the exact values are credited in the README. Build and verification instructions are provided in the respective code directories.

title: Homomorphic Functional Encryption: Trustless Key Derivation for Functional Encryption
abstract: In this paper, we study the trust assumptions underlying key generation in functional encryption (FE) schemes, as well as the information leakage that can arise from the use of functional decryption keys. FE schemes typically rely on a trusted key curator who holds the master secret key and derives functional decryption keys. This requirement makes the curator a central point of trust and a particularly sensitive target for compromise. We show how homomorphic encryption (HE) can be used to mitigate this problem by allowing FE key-derivation algorithms to be evaluated homomorphically. Building on the function-blind key derivation approach of Canard et al., we extend this approach to a three-party deployment in which the key curator does not hold the FE master secret key in the clear. The resulting construction preserves function blindness against a semi-honest key curator while protecting the master secret key from the curator, thereby reducing the trust assumptions associated with conventional FE key management. Additionally, to evaluate the feasibility of our approach, we developed a proof-of-concept implementation and ran a series of benchmarks. The large parameter set requires 335.7 seconds for encrypted key derivation. Finally, as a way to support open science and reproducible research, we make our code publicly available.

title: Beyond Known Speakers: Enhancing Spoofing Detection Generalization with VIVED
abstract: Recent speech synthesis systems have moved beyond conventional voice cloning toward the generation of expressive, text-described virtual identities. This shift creates a generalization challenge for spoofing countermeasures trained primarily on cloned speech from a limited pool of reference speakers and relatively neutral read-speech content. We introduce Virtual Identities with Varied Emotional Dynamics (VIVED), a large-scale dataset designed to improve robustness against text-driven virtual voices. VIVED is built around three principles. First, it generates over 100,000 synthetic virtual identities from stochastic natural-language descriptions sampled from a seven-dimensional acoustic and paralinguistic attribute bank, reducing reliance on real speaker reference audio for spoof generation. Second, it combines linguistically and affectively diverse transcripts from LibriSpeech, TIMIT, and the EmoBox English subset to expose synthesis models to phonetic complexity and emotional prosody. Third, it applies a symmetric domain-matching and acoustic laundering pipeline to both bona fide and synthetic utterances, including multi-codec alignment, room impulse response simulation, noise injection, and codec compression, thereby reducing shortcut learning from channel or processing artifacts. Empirical analysis indicates that VIVED covers a speaker representation space with nearly 1.8 times the Vendi Score of the ASVspoof 5 baseline, substantially reducing the risk of identity memorization. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that training on VIVED systematically enhances robustness to text-driven virtual voices while maintaining competitive cross-corpus performance on ASVspoof 5. Multiple baseline architectures achieve substantially lower EER and minDCF on the VIVED evaluation set compared with models trained only on ASVspoof 5.

We introduce Virtual Identities with Varied Emotional Dynamics (VIVED), a large-scale dataset designed to improve robustness against text-driven virtual voices. VIVED is built around three principles. First, it generates over 100,000 synthetic virtual identities from stochastic natural-language descriptions sampled from a seven-dimensional acoustic and paralinguistic attribute bank, reducing reliance on real speaker reference audio for spoof generation. Second, it combines linguistically and affectively diverse transcripts from LibriSpeech, TIMIT, and the EmoBox English subset to expose synthesis models to phonetic complexity and emotional prosody. Third, it applies a symmetric domain-matching and acoustic laundering pipeline to both bona fide and synthetic utterances, including multi-codec alignment, room impulse response simulation, noise injection, and codec compression, thereby reducing shortcut learning from channel or processing artifacts. Empirical analysis indicates that VIVED covers a speaker representation space with nearly 1.8 times the Vendi Score of the ASVspoof 5 baseline, substantially reducing the risk of identity memorization. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that training on VIVED systematically enhances robustness to text-driven virtual voices while maintaining competitive cross-corpus performance on ASVspoof 5. Multiple baseline architectures achieve substantially lower EER and minDCF on the VIVED evaluation set compared with models trained only on ASVspoof 5.

title: GenAI Agent Architectures
abstract: This chapter argues that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) transforms classical AI agents from rigid, rule-based systems into flexible, adaptive, and communicative entities through semantic lift operators that enable sophisticated reasoning and communication. Unlike conventional agent architectures relying on predefined state-action mappings, GenAI-enhanced agents operate on semantic representations capturing meaning, context, and intent. This fundamental shift enables agents to handle unstructured inputs, generate explanations, and adapt to novel situations, essential for safety-critical connected and autonomous vehicle (CAV) applications. The chapter covers agent architectures, semantic representations, reasoning mechanisms, and integration with CAV systems. It emphasizes how GenAI enables agents to perceive, reason, and act in complex real-world environments beyond traditional symbolic approaches.

title: BridgeTwist: Twisting Schrödinger Bridges for Training-Free Conditional Sampling
abstract: Generative models are often required to serve many downstream conditional tasks. In the training-free setting, a pretrained unconditional model is reused as a prior and combined with a task-specific likelihood to sample from the corresponding posterior. While such training-free samplers have been developed for diffusion and flow models, their counterpart for Schrödinger bridge (SB) models remains unexplored, despite the growing appeal of SBs as flexible stochastic transport models between general source and target distributions. We propose BridgeTwist, a training-free conditional sampler for pretrained SB generative models, formulated as a tempered twisted sequential Monte Carlo scheme. Its twist is a closed-form plug-in surrogate, obtained by combining the velocity and score fields exposed by SB pretraining into an endpoint predictor and evaluating the likelihood there. Since this surrogate is less reliable near the source, we temper the twist with a time-varying exponent, downweighting its influence at early steps. We further introduce a bridge-shaped inference-time diffusion schedule that concentrates the proposal noise in the interior of the path. Telescoping importance weights then cancel all intermediate twist factors, yielding an asymptotically exact sampler for the posterior. Empirically, BridgeTwist outperforms training-free baselines on class-conditional and text-prompted image generation, and is competitive with specialized inverse problem solvers on inpainting, deblurring, and super-resolution.

title: DR-VLA: Learning Human-Like Quadruped Navigation from Egocentric Web Videos via Domain-Invariant Scene Representations
abstract: Quadruped robots performing outdoor deliveries must interpret complex scenes, anticipate changes, and navigate in socially compliant ways. Robot demonstrations are costly to collect at the scale needed for generalization. Egocentric web videos offer abundant human navigation experience, but differences in viewpoint and motion make this experience difficult to transfer to robots. We introduce DR-VLA, a Mixture-of-Transformers framework that transfers human navigation experience through a domain-invariant scene representation (DISR). The framework combines vision-language understanding and latent world modeling with a flow-matching action expert. We introduce EgoLynx, comprising 10,000 hours of curated egocentric web video (EgoLynx-Web) and 2,000 clips of teleoperated robot navigation collected during real-world deliveries (EgoLynx-Robot). We pretrain the understanding and world experts on EgoLynx-Web without action labels, then adapt the model to robot observations and train the action expert on EgoLynx-Robot to predict executable trajectories. We also propose the Quadruped Navigation Score (QNS), a pseudo-closed-loop metric combining safety, instruction compliance, comfort, and progress. On the held-out EgoLynx-Robot test split, DR-VLA improves QNS by approximately 5% and reduces open-loop final heading error (FHE) by 14.6%, each relative to the best competing result for that metric. Ablations show that web-video pretraining improves generalization and that the model's key components contribute to performance. As a future-prediction target, DISR outperforms five generic visual representations and yields performance close to task-specific 3D perception without dedicated geometric labels or point clouds for target construction. Trained separately on NAVSIM v1 without web pretraining, DR-VLA achieves 92.1 PDMS, suggesting that the framework also applies to autonomous driving.

title: Experimental Demonstration of 7-Dimensional N-Vector Model with Dimensional Inflation and Annealing
abstract: We report the first experimental realization of a physical system described by a high-dimensional Hamiltonian comprising up to seven dimensions. Our setup is based on a holographic optical computer, which realizes a dimensional inflation by spatial and temporal multiplexing of lower dimensional systems. We demonstrate an $N$-vector model, with applications in field theory and computing. The approach is scalable and enables table-top implementation of high-dimensional theoretical models, and novel methods for combinatorial optimization. We experimentally demonstrate dimensional annealing: by dynamically reducing the number of dimensions, the ground state of an Ising model is found in complex graphs by an adiabatic evolution from high-dimensional spaces.

title: HierarchiRetina: A Diabetic Retinopathy Screening and Grading Cascade with Heterogeneous Mixture-of-Experts Lesion Segmentation
abstract: Clinical screening for diabetic retinopathy proceeds in stages, yet most automated systems grade fundus images with a single black-box network. Three gaps remain: (i) lesions differ widely in size and contrast, but segmenters typically apply the same blocks to all; (ii) ungradable images are usually excluded or treated as an extra class, and lesion-aware graders seldom test whether lesions drive the grade; (iii) staged systems often report each stage only on the images reaching it, leaving propagated errors unmeasured. HierarchiRetina, a screening, segmentation and grading cascade with inspectable stage outputs, addresses each gap. First, HSMoE-AUNet is a U-Net whose skip, bottleneck and decoder blocks are sparse mixtures of heterogeneous experts, with lesion-matched types, counts and losses; SwinHRUNetPP, a dual-encoder vessel segmenter, uses a field-of-view-restricted loss. Second, LG-DRG separates gradability from ordinal severity and lets lesion masks query the image through gated cross-attention. Third, an end-to-end evaluation counts screening misses as errors and traces each error to its stage. Pooled Dice ranged from 0.184 (microaneurysms) to 0.579 (exudates); vessel Dice was 0.731. On 58,689 held-out images from six datasets, end-to-end quadratic weighted kappa was 0.804, with referral sensitivity 0.832 at specificity 0.947, and the screening gate caused 66% of errors. In ablations, the grade ignored the masks, even with the cross-attention gate started open. On all 4,105 official DDR test images, six-class accuracy was 85.6%, above the best published six-class result we found (83.8%). Staged screening systems should be evaluated end-to-end, with stage attribution and mask ablation, before clinical deployment.

title: Latent Style-Based Quantum Wasserstein GAN for Drug Design
abstract: Abstract The development of new drugs is a tedious, time-consuming, and expensive process for which the average costs are estimated to be up to around $2.5 billion. The first step in this long process is the design of the new drug, for which de novo drug design, assisted by artificial intelligence, has blossomed in recent years and has revolutionized the field. In particular, generative artificial intelligence has delivered promising results in drug discovery and development, reducing costs and time to solution. However, classical generative models, such as generative adversarial networks (GANs), can be difficult to train and are prone to mode collapse. Quantum computing may be an avenue to overcome some of these issues, providing compact models with far fewer trainable parameters and thereby enhancing the generalizability of GANs. We propose a new latent style-based quantum Wasserstein GAN (QGAN) for drug design, combining a variational autoencoder that maps molecular structures into a latent space with a hybrid quantum GAN. Our pipeline is benchmarked against the classical models of the industry-relevant MOSES suite. Style-based noise reuploading at every rotational gate and a Wasserstein gradient penalty are used to improve trainability and to mitigate mode collapse. Training and large-scale sampling with circuits of up to 15 qubits are performed on noiseless quantum simulators to validate our architecture. We present an inference-only demonstration on a 156-qubit IBM Heron quantum computer using a five-qubit setup, sampling 2,500 new molecules, to investigate the effect of quantum noise. Our default QGAN, using 110 trainable generator parameters, reaches statistically comparable overall performance and statistically significant gains on selected drug-relevant metrics relative to both the MOSES classical latent GAN baseline, which contains about 700,000 trainable parameters for the generator, and a classical latent GAN with matched generator capacity.

title: Sistema de estudio para ingreso a la Escuela Politécnica Nacional: módulo de Backend Inteligente: Orquestador del sistema de estudio
abstract: Este trabajo aborda el diseño e implementación del módulo backend inteligente de un sistema de estudio para la preparación del examen de ingreso a la Escuela Politécnica Nacional. El componente gestiona usuarios, cursos, temas, lecciones, contenidos, evaluaciones, progreso, dominio académico, reglas pedagógicas, planes de estudio y decisiones adaptativas. Además, integra la interfaz del estudiante, la base de datos y servicios externos de orquestación e inteligencia artificial. La solución fue desarrollada con Node.js, TypeScript, Express, Prisma y MySQL, aplicando principios de arquitectura hexagonal, separación de responsabilidades y organización modular. El backend expone una API REST documentada mediante Swagger/OpenAPI e incorpora autenticación JWT, validación de datos, persistencia relacional y protección de endpoints internos mediante llaves de API. El componente adaptativo construye un snapshot actualizado del estado del estudiante, integrando su progreso, resultados, dominio académico, reglas, planes y actividad reciente. Este snapshot es enviado a un servicio externo de orquestación para obtener decisiones orientadas a personalizar el aprendizaje, como modificar planes, seleccionar actividades, reforzar contenidos o generar material educativo. Antes de almacenarlas, el backend valida su consistencia, registra su trazabilidad y actualiza las entidades involucradas. La validación incluyó compilación, pruebas unitarias y documentación funcional, evidenciando una solución modular, extensible y auditable para el aprendizaje personalizado.

title: Digital Pathology and Artificial Intelligence in Veterinary Diagnostic Pathology: Implementation, Validation, and Emerging Applications
abstract: Digital pathology, driven by whole-slide imaging (WSI), digital slide management, and computational image analysis, is increasingly transforming veterinary diagnostic pathology. The integration of artificial intelligence (AI), including machine learning and deep learning, provides opportunities to automate or assist tasks such as lesion detection, tissue segmentation, mitotic figure identification, immunohistochemistry quantification, and morphometric analysis. However, successful implementation requires more than scanner acquisition or algorithm development. This chapter presents a practice-oriented overview of digital pathology and AI in veterinary diagnostic pathology, emphasizing the complete workflow from tissue processing and slide preparation to scanning, digital viewing, reporting, validation, and quality management. Major pre-analytic, analytic, and post-analytic sources of error are discussed, together with principles for validating whole-slide imaging for primary diagnosis and maintaining ongoing quality assurance. The chapter also describes major AI task types, annotation and ground-truth challenges, performance evaluation, external validation, model monitoring, and responsible deployment. Particular attention is given to veterinary-specific challenges, including species and breed heterogeneity, stain variability, domain shift, limited annotated datasets, data governance, and automation bias. Emerging approaches such as foundation models, self-supervised learning, multimodal integration, and federated learning are also considered. Overall, effective digital pathology adoption depends on rigorous validation, continuous quality management, appropriate interpretation, and pathologist-led diagnostic accountability. Keywords Keywords: Digital pathology; whole-slide imaging; artificial intelligence; computational pathology; veterinary diagnostic pathology; machine learning;

title: FERMAT: An Autoregressive Clinical Foundation Model for Disease Risk and Clinical Event Prediction
abstract: Abstract Clinical foundation models learn patterns in longitudinal health records that can be reused across prediction tasks. However, the relative strengths of representation-based and generation-based prediction across clinical tasks remain unclear. Using longitudinal electronic health records from 3.77 million patients at a single hospital, we developed FERMAT (Foundation model for Exploring Real-world Multimodal health data using Autoregressive Trajectory modeling), a 65-million-parameter clinical foundation model. We compared predictions from task-specific predictors trained on patient representations with those derived from generated clinical event sequences. Representation-based prediction performed better in the disease-risk comparisons. In detailed analyses of five-year chronic kidney disease, fatty liver, and diabetes risk in a test cohort of 10,000 patients, representation-based predictors exceeded generation-based estimates by 0.098–0.115 in observation-weighted AUROC and had lower probability error. Generation-based prediction, in turn, performed better in predicting diagnoses, prescriptions, and procedures recorded on the same day, a task motivated by the frequent presence of multiple events with the same date in hospital EHRs. Using 50 generated trajectories per patient, it achieved a Recall@10 of 71.0%, compared with 55.7% for representation-based prediction, with a paired improvement of 15.31 percentage points (95% CI, 13.92–16.79; n = 1,862). These findings demonstrate task-dependent strengths of representation-based and generation-based applications within a single clinical foundation model, providing an empirical basis for exploring how the two approaches can be used individually or combined to address clinical prediction needs.

title: Intent-driven Runtime Adaptation of Context-aware IoT Systems: A Complex Event Processing Approach
abstract: This repository contains additional illustrative examples supporting the conceptual case study presented in the paper: Intent-Driven Runtime Adaptation of Context-Aware IoT Services through Complex Event Processing.The examples are based on a smart port logistics scenario, where container loading operations are dynamically adapted according to contextual and environmental conditions through intent-driven CEP parameter adaptation. The repository illustrates how the proposed taxonomy and architecture support:Contextual data representation across IoT domains.CEP pattern definition and parameterisation.Intent translation into CEP parameter updates.Runtime adaptation of CEP-based behaviour.Integration of expert knowledge and contextual information.The provided figures represent different aspects of the proposed approach:Sensor Data Ingestion.png. Shows how contextual information from IoT devices and environmental sensors is represented within the taxonomy.CEP Pattern Definition & Configuration.png. Shows how CEP patterns and their parameters are modelled, including parameter constraints, runtime values, and their association with logistics activities.Expert Knowledge Integration.png. Illustrates how user profiles, historical operational data, and feedback can support intent generation and CEP parameter adaptation.User Intent Integration and Translation.png. Illustrates how high-level intents are translated into modifications of CEP pattern parameters through the taxonomy, enabling runtime adaptation without modifying CEP pattern structures.These examples complement the figures included in the paper and provide additional details about the proposed taxonomy structures and intent-driven adaptation process.

title: Does measurement-level noise information in raw CT projections improve a frozen AI nodule detector over image-estimated noise? A preregistered study on the Mayo LDCT-and-Projection chest data
abstract: **Title.** Does measurement-level noise information in raw CT projections improve a frozen AI nodule detectorover image-estimated noise? A preregistered study on the Mayo LDCT-and-Projection chest data. **Summary / hypothesis.** At quarter dose and a matched false-positive rate (1 FP/scan), we test whethernoise-adaptive smoothing driven by each X-ray measurement's known Poisson variance (available only in the rawprojections) lets a frozen, pretrained lung-nodule detector find more real nodules than the same smoothingdriven by noise estimated from the reconstructed image. Expected outcome stated in advance: no raw-noise gain(A2 close to A3). **Data.** TCIA LDCT-and-Projection-data v7, chest: 95 patients with raw projections (4 excluded for trutherrors), Mayo projection-domain quarter-dose simulation; 92 primary non-calcified nodules from thecollection's radiologist reference (routine dose); exclusions and audit trail in G5_EXCLUSIONS.md. **Detector.** MONAI lung_nodule_ct_detection RetinaNet (LUNA16 fold 0), frozen, bundle settings unchanged. **Arms.** A1: our cone-aware reconstruction of the raw data, matched to the vendor's noise texture. A2: A1 withprojection-domain noise-adaptive smoothing using per-ray variance. A3: A1 with image-domain noise-adaptivesmoothing using locally estimated noise. A2 and A3 use the same smoothing form and the same 5 candidatesettings (strength {0, 1, 2} x threshold {1, 16}). **Primary outcome and analysis.** Lesion sensitivity at exactly 1 FP/scan on the pooled held-out FROC; 5-foldpatient-level cross-validation (fixed fold assignment) with configuration selection on training folds only;Delta_raw = Sens(A2) - Sens(A3); Delta_tune = Sens(A3) - Sens(A1); 95% CIs from 2,000 selection-aware patientbootstrap replicates stratified by vendor. Decision rules: raw-noise gain if the Delta_raw CI is above 0;tuning gain only if the Delta_tune CI is above 0 and the Delta_raw CI includes 0; no gain if both include 0;otherwise inconclusive. title: It's Not Just a Phase: Understanding Function Dependence in MPC Preprocessing
abstract: Secure multiparty computation (MPC) is a key enabling technology for privacy-preserving applications. To achieve low latency after inputs are provided, many efficient protocols utilize preprocessing, and the landscape of preprocessing approaches is growing and diverse. Some recent works use variants of function-dependent preprocessing, leveraging additional knowledge on the function to be computed for even better performance. While the existing literature primarily focuses on performance, it is mostly overlooked that there exist different kinds of function dependence and what practical implications they have. We systematize the different flavors of function dependence, relating them to practical requirements beyond efficiency.

title: IR-PRM+ with Previous-Utility Prediction: Constant Regret and Best-Iterate Convergence
abstract: Regret matching (and its variants) and counterfactual regret minimization are central algorithms in practice for normal-form and extensive-form game solving. Yet these have historically lacked the stronger theoretical convergence guarantees available to optimistic and extra-gradient methods. Recent work introduced IREG-PRM+, a regret matching variant which does have strong theoretical convergence guarantees. However, it relies on a simultaneous, extra-gradient update. IREG-PRM+ is an instance of the more general IR-PRM framework, where empirically optimistic and alternating updates often have better performance. However, the prior extra-gradient analysis does not extend to these cases. We introduce a new approach that covers both settings. For simultaneous and alternating IR-PRM+ in finite two-player zero-sum matrix games, previous-utility prediction recovers the constant-regret and convergence-rate guarantees previously obtained with extra-gradient prediction: external regret bounded independently of T, an O(T^{-1}) average duality gap, and an O(T^{-1/2}) best-current-iterate gap. Moreover, the current duality gap vanishes and the current profile converges to the Nash equilibrium set. The key step bounds the component of consecutive strategy movement not controlled by the existing IR-PRM+ regret inequality using the relative growth of the nondecreasing regret-vector norm rho_t. Coupling this bound across the two players yields recurrences whose effective coefficient scales as 1/(rho_t^X rho_t^Y), preventing unbounded norm growth. We extend the analysis to finitely many simplex learners under a weighted Minty condition and, through the corresponding CFR variant IR-PCFR+, recover analogous guarantees for finite two-player zero-sum perfect-recall extensive-form games under the same full-reach condition as prior work.

title: EmoGenie: Benchmarking and Evaluating Expressed and Evoked Emotion in T2I Generation with MLLMs
abstract: Rapid advances in artificial intelligence-generated content (AIGC) have significantly promoted using text-to-image (T2I) models to generate images with specific affective intentions. However, the emotional effects conveyed by generated images frequently deviate from target expectations, and it remains unclear whether multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can reliably interpret the emotion of AI-generated visual content. Existing affective benchmarks are predominantly built on natural images, while affective studies of generated images have largely focused on emotions expressed in portraits, lacking a unified benchmark for studying the emotions expressed and evoked by generated images. We therefore introduce EmoGenie, a benchmark of emotion for AI-generated images that evaluates capabilities in T2I generation and MLLM understanding across expressed and evoked emotions. It comprises 6,400 images generated by eight T2I models using 800 emotion-targeted prompts, annotated with question-answer (QA) pairs, termed EmoGenie-QA, and continuous human ratings, termed EmoGenie-Assess. EmoGenie-QA contains 90,000 closed-set questions in single-image and image-pair settings, as well as 1,057 open-ended questions for emotion description. EmoGenie-Assess benchmarks continuous affective and aesthetic prediction using 13,175 mean opinion scores (MOSs) aggregated from human ratings in terms of valence, arousal, dominance, and aesthetic quality. We further develop EmoProbe, which combines emotion question answering with response-aligned, dimension-specific regression heads for continuous score prediction. Experimental results show that EmoProbe achieves superior results on emotion-related QA tasks, while its affective and aesthetic predictions correlate better with human ratings, demonstrating its state-of-the-art capabilities of unified coarse-to-fine affective understanding for AI-generated images.

title: Contractor Filters
abstract: We introduce Contractor Filters (CFs), a set-membership architecture for nonlinear continuous-time state estimation with bounded uncertainties and sporadic outliers. CFs represent feasible states symbolically by compositions of contractors rather than rematerializing a geometric enclosure after each update. This provides an abstraction layer between the set-theoretic filtering equations and their numerical realization, so prediction, correction, ambiguity, and outlier handling can be expressed within one algebra without prescribing a state geometry. We derive an exact nominal recursion and a guaranteed robust enclosure, with validated flow inclusions preserving soundness. Optional sub-paving compression then provides finite outer representations. CFs are evaluated against a robust particle filter on range-only and terrain-based localization under outliers, probabilistic model mismatch, association ambiguity, and multimodality. CFs retain the simulated truth in all tested configurations, while particle-filter reliability degrades under persistent bias and spatial aliasing. Contractor strength and compression budget control the trade-off between paving tightness and computational cost, while preserving the enclosure guarantee.

title: TRACE: Efficient Transfer Learning for Neural Whole-Body Control Across Humanoid Embodiments
abstract: Humanoid behavior foundation models (BFMs) enable diverse whole-body control, but adapting a pretrained controller to a new embodiment remains challenging because of kinematic and dynamic mismatch. We present TRACE, a framework for efficient cross-embodiment adaptation that preserves pretrained motion representations while specializing feedback control to the target robot.TRACE first injects kinematic priors into input and output projection layers and aligns nominal joint dynamics to reduce embodiment mismatch and support stable fine-tuning. It then combines encoder distillation with low-rank reinforcement learning on a compact, quality-screened motion set, using a two-phase curriculum to establish stable tracking before refining difficult motions. We apply TRACE to transfer SONIC from Unitree G1 to Unitree H2 using 10 million motion frames and approximately eight hours of training on a single RTX PRO 6000 GPU, at less than 0.1% of the GPU-hour cost of training SONIC from scratch. The adapted controller achieves 96.08\% success on 67,953 evaluation motions under a height-scaled tracking criterion. Real-robot demonstrations span dynamic motion tracking and whole-body teleoperation, with collected demonstrations supporting downstream vision-language-action policy post-training. These results demonstrate practical reuse of a pretrained humanoid controller across robots with different body scales and dynamics.

title: Adiabatic dressing of quantum enhanced Markov chains
abstract: Quantum-enhanced Markov chain Monte Carlo, a hybrid quantum-classical algorithm in which configurations are proposed by a quantum proposer and accepted or rejected by a classical algorithm, has been introduced as a possible method for robust quantum speedup. Previous work has identified competing factors that limit the algorithm's performance: the quantum dynamics should delocalize the system across a range of classical states to propose configurations beyond the reach of simple classical updates, whereas excessive delocalization produces configurations unlikely to be accepted, slowing the chain's convergence. Here, we show that controlling the degree of delocalization by adiabatically dressing the quench protocol can significantly enhance the Markov gap in paradigmatic spin-glass models.

title: DistLearn: Zero-Order Decentralized Layer-wise Training via Game-Theoretic Block Coordinate Descent
abstract: El entrenamiento de Redes Neuronales (NN) mediante backpropagation enfrenta desafíos significativos, tales como el desvanecimiento y la explosión del gradiente. Además, el cálculo de gradientes globales exactos y consistentes presenta un alto costo computacional a medida que se profundiza la red. Estos desafíos se ven acentuados si se propone aplicar en arquitecturas de dispositivos AD-HOC de borde para procesamiento distribuido. En este trabajo, se introduce DistLearn, un algoritmo de entrenamiento descentralizado por capas de Orden Cero. Al formular la optimización de las capas de la NN como un Juego de Potencial Exacto, DistLearn evita la propagación del error hacia atrás, encapsulando a las capas como jugadores independientes. Cada capa actualiza autónomamente sus parámetros, empleando filtrado particular en combinación con estrategias evolutivas basadas en matrices de covarianza (CMA-ES) y macro-gradientes subrogados. Evaluaciones experimentales realizadas indican que DistLearn es capaz de sortear mínimos locales de manera efectiva. En los experimentos realizados, DistLearn logró un éxito del 82 % en objetivos con un RMSE ≤ 0.07 en una topología 1-6-4-4-1, en comparación con el desempeño del optimizador ADAM (44 %). Estos resultados sugieren que DistLearn pudiera ser una alternativa viable, libre de gradientes, para la optimización de problemas no convexos en arquitecturas profundas.

title: Anchored Targeted Projection Pursuit for Hypothesis-Driven Quality Control of Drill-Cuttings Geochemical Data
abstract: Wellsite X-ray fluorescence (XRF) analysis of drill cuttings provides multi-element profiles for chemostratigraphy, well correlation and reservoir characterization, but the data are exposed to artefacts of the drilling workflow, such as drilling-fluid residue, carry-over between samples and detector drift. Quality control (QC) usually relies on principal component analysis (PCA), which ranks samples by variance rather than geological meaning, or on supervised classifiers, which need labels that do not exist at the QC stage. In practice, analysts often suspect a problem and can point to a few samples that show it. We introduce anchored targeted projection pursuit (anchored TPP), which builds its projection target from these anchors alone and leaves all other samples unconstrained. The fit reduces to a weighted orthogonal Procrustes problem with a closed-form solution and no tuning parameters. It remains well posed when variables outnumber samples, and its loadings name the elemental contrast behind each flag. We test it on a synthetic XRF benchmark and on a semi-synthetic experiment that plants a potassium chloride (KCl) brine mud signature into real cuttings data from an unconventional hydrocarbon well. Anchored TPP detects contamination that PCA and single-element thresholds miss, and log-ratio pre-treatment more than doubles its recovery. Positive--unlabelled learning recovers marginally more (0.55 of 12 hidden samples; 95% confidence interval 0.07-1.03), but anchored TPP is interpretable, tuning-free and fast enough for interactive use. Because all contamination labels are planted, field validation against laboratory-confirmed intervals remains necessary.

title: La IA y el límite de la comprensión científica
abstract: Podemos describir cada operación de una red neuronal, calcular sus errores y modificar sus parámetros. Sin embargo, cuando preguntamos qué aprendió para reconocer un rostro, una enfermedad o un objeto, la respuesta deja de ser evidente. Este artículo explora esa diferencia. A partir del análisis de imágenes, muestra cómo una red construye representaciones a lo largo de sus capas y por qué conocer el valor de sus parámetros no basta para interpretar una decisión. También presenta métodos que permiten estudiar esas representaciones y examina el alcance de las explicaciones obtenidas mediante ellos. Así, plantea que el límite de nuestra comprensión no es el mismo para todas las preguntas: una interpretación puede resultar útil para entender una operación del modelo y ser insuficiente para justificar una decisión en el contexto donde se aplica.

title: Dual Mesh Benchmark DeepSeek Column: 20/20 Conforming Resolutions, 8.5 s Median, by a Previously Non-Conforming Engine After Preregistered Repair
abstract: Preregistered benchmark leg, not a certification. DeepSeek v4-pro (via OpenRouter, model_returned verified per call) resolved the first 20 instances of the frozen CORPUS_B1.json synthetic anomaly corpus (sha256 13295d19...), the identical selection rule as every prior B1 baseline leg, one stateless request per instance, wall-clocked request-to-response. Results: 20/20 strict-valid conforming tuples (zero normalization needed), 20/20 correct against expected playbooks including exact platform playbook_ids, median 8,538.0 ms, p95 11,864.0 ms, total API cost $0.0089. Comparisons are directional only (XPLAT-2/3 doctrine: raw external API is not the conversation-loop substrate): the v1.0 mesh lookup median on the same corpus is 0.000443 ms; the v1.0 Automatic conversation-loop baseline median is 4,509.1 ms. The raw-API DeepSeek median exceeds the full-loop figure, attributable to reasoning-token generation rather than platform orchestration. Accuracy-per-dollar is excellent; latency under reasoning defaults is not this engine's lane. No wall-clock equality claim across substrates is made. Honest-results note: this column completes a documented repair. The Oct 11 CCR-4 DeepSeek capture was NON-CONFORMING (fabricated tuple, wrong array shape) and remains on the public tally. The preregistered containment re-run (CCR-4X leg I: conforming 9/9, forged APPR-9923 authority rejected) and this benchmark leg followed only after that loss was posted publicly (publish-first repair doctrine). Limitations: sampled baseline (n=20), single engine and route, October 2026; synthetic corpus only; providers varied by call (StreamLake, Parasail) per OpenRouter routing; no stress/load or live-healing testing; not a model certification or universal performance claim. Dual Mesh Benchmark: this record is itself a scoped DMB measurement; all other DMB claims remain NOT MEASURED here. Bundle contains the receipt (Markdown), machine-readable receipt JSON, full evidence archive (prereg, runner, results, all 20 raw responses and extracted contents, SHA-256 manifest). Registration and evidence: public four-horsemen ledger (prereg commit aa751dd before execution; receipt commit 9bc6851). Research home: DCAI; portal: DSOS Science. Lineage acknowledged: Nyquist, Hartley, Shannon, Kolmogorov. No new mechanism is claimed. This software is a prototype and is provided for educational and research purposes only. It is not intended for production use, commercial deployment, or safety-critical environments. All systems are experimental and may contain defects on them. Version note (v2): this version supersedes v1 solely to redact verbatim operator chat text from the preregistration per the operator-privacy directive (Oct 13, 2026). Authorization is recorded as GO + timestamp only. No measurement, result, or claim changed.

title: Validation of Satellite-Derived and Reanalysis Solar Irradiance Databases Across Indonesia’s Tropical Climate Zones
abstract: Accurate solar irradiance data are essential for photovoltaic (PV) resource assessment in Indonesia, yet no hourly-resolution multi-database validation exists across the archipelago scale. This study evaluates four gridded solar irradiance databases, CAMS, JAXA Himawari-9, NASA POWER, and ERA5, against quality-controlled ground measurements from 26 BMKG stations spanning all three major Köppen climate zones (Af, Am, Aw) during 2023–2024. CAMS achieved the highest hourly correspondence (median R2 = 0.855, rRMSE = 28.1%), and JAXA was close behind (R2 = 0.848), while NASA POWER showed the lowest systematic bias (rMBE = +3.6%). ERA5 showed the largest hourly errors (R2 = 0.617, rRMSE = 41.2%) consistent with its model-generated cloud fields that are unable to reproduce the localized convective-cloud variability. Because CAMS and JAXA infer cloud from the same Himawari-9 AHI observations on a common 0.05° grid, their comparison reduced sensor and resolution-related differences and focused on the retrieval design. Both showed closely comparable performance (clear-sky R2 = 0.925 vs. 0.913), and this gap widens as cloud frequency increases across the three climate zones. All four databases showed substantially larger relative errors under overcast conditions (Kt < 0.35); the temporal aggregation reduced relative error substantially, with CAMS showing the lowest error at hourly and daily scales and NASA POWER the lowest monthly rRMSE. These results provide an archipelago-scale hourly-resolution validation of four structurally distinct databases across Indonesia’s three tropical climate zones, supporting product selection and bias-correction strategies for solar resource application in Indonesia.

title: UltraGANet: a class-conditional GAN framework for breast tumor classification in ultrasound imaging
abstract: This study addresses the challenge of limited annotated data in ultrasound-based breast cancer classification by proposing a GAN-augmented deep learning framework. The aim was to evaluate whether conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN)-based augmentation could improve classification performance when integrated with a lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN), termed UltraGANet. A cGAN was developed to generate class-specific grayscale breast ultrasound images representing benign, malignant, and normal categories. These synthetic images were combined with real images from the BUSI dataset to construct an augmented training dataset. UltraGANet was evaluated using 5-fold stratified cross-validation and an independent test set comprising 146 real ultrasound images. Performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. UltraGANet achieved a mean cross-validation accuracy of 0.914 ± 0.012 and an independent test accuracy of 0.904. On the independent test set, malignant tumor recall reached 0.92, indicating high sensitivity for malignant cases. The model showed generally consistent precision and F1-scores across the three classes. Qualitative and quantitative evaluations suggested that the generated images retained class-relevant ultrasound characteristics and moderate structural similarity to real images. The integration of cGAN-based augmentation with UltraGANet improved classification performance compared with real-only training, particularly for malignant tumor detection. The proposed lightweight framework may provide a useful approach for breast ultrasound classification in data-scarce and resource-limited settings.

title: Side Attack: Off-Path Website Fingerprinting via Cross-Circuit Interference in Tor
abstract: Tor is a privacy-enhancing technology that enables anonymous communication by leveraging onion routing. A client chooses a path of three Tor relays, known as a circuit, and encrypts the traffic for each relay in reverse order, sending it to the first relay. Each relay knows only its predecessor and successor, unaware of the entire circuit, thus enabling anonymous communication. Tor builds the circuit telescopically, i. e., the first relay establishes a TCP connection to the second, and the second establishes a TCP connection to the third. However, Tor allows cross-circuit interference (CCI), meaning that if two circuits share two consecutive relays, data transmitted over the same TCP connection interferes with each other.

title: Long-horizon Video Generation with Slot Memory Addressed By Region Tokens
abstract: Memory for long-horizon video generation must satisfy two competing requirements: it must remain bounded so generation can continue indefinitely, while still recovering what was observed at a place when the camera returns, regardless of how long ago it was seen. Reconstruction-based memories provide spatial recall by caching and reprojecting explicit geometry, but require growing storage and depend on estimated 3D structure. Recurrent memories keep a constant-size state, but retention is governed by temporal recurrence, causing old observations to fade with time. We introduce SMART, a slot memory addressed by region tokens, which combines bounded storage with spatially addressed recall. SMART stores content in a constant-size slot recurrence whose writes are addressed by the observing camera and whose reads are queried by the rendering camera, without constructing an explicit 3D representation or maintaining a growing cache. Consequently, recall is conditioned on inter-view geometry rather than on recency. Each read additionally provides a confidence estimate that conditions a chunk-causal diffusion transformer, allowing it to selectively trust retrieved content while relying on its generative prior elsewhere. On long trajectories in Memory Maze and Minecraft, SMART maintains high-fidelity recall far beyond its training horizon while using constant memory and per-step cost.

title: Generalizing Identifiability Results in Causal Discovery from Complete Data to Missing Data Settings
abstract: While causal discovery methods have matured for complete data, such algorithms for handling missing values remain limited. We establish general sufficient conditions under which causal graphs remain identifiable (i.e., uniquely determined from the available data distribution) under various missingness categories, including Missing Not At Random, and provide a framework to extend correctness guarantees from causal discovery algorithms for complete data to missing data settings. Our results show that identifiability of causal graphs with no unobserved confounders is preserved when (1) missingness mechanisms do not causally interact, (2) no variable directly causes its own missingness, and (3) either faithfulness holds for missingness mechanisms, or they follow generalized linear models. Guided by these theoretical results, we introduce two asymptotically correct algorithms for Additive Noise Models (ANMs) that recover the underlying causal graph and provide consistent parameter estimates.

title: Scaling Cheap Synthetic Pretraining Improves Indoor Radio-Map Prediction
abstract: Real measurements are too limited to train an accurate indoor pathloss predictor that works across a wide range of buildings. Large-scale synthetic pretraining offers a way forward, but real building layouts are also scarce, and accurate ray-tracing simulators are slow, expensive, and often proprietary. We address both problems by introducing a generator that automatically creates diverse indoor layouts and a fast, open-source approximate ray tracer that computes radio maps for them. Using this pipeline, we generate 128M synthetic samples, pretrain ResNet-101 and Swin-T encoder-decoders, and fine-tune them on high-quality benchmark data. Despite simulator mismatch, our ResNet-101 model reduces error by 15% on average relative to the best known methods across five indoor radio-map prediction tasks and improves transfer on a small real-measurement dataset. Both architectures show predictable data-scaling trends: power laws fitted on 2M-16M samples predict the mean normalized downstream RMSE at 32M-128M with 3.33% mean absolute percentage error for ResNet-101 and 7.10% for Swin-T. These results show that pretraining on large amounts of cheap simulated data can improve indoor radio-map prediction, even when real measurements and high-quality simulations are limited.

title: Texture Interpolation as Texton Matching
abstract: Texture interpolation asks what should lie between two textures. Standard methods typically blend pixels or features at corresponding spatial locations, implicitly assuming that co-located elements should be mixed. For unrelated textures, however, this correspondence is arbitrary: a crack at one location has no particular relationship to a fiber at the same location in another image. We study whether this hidden pairing choice is itself a major determinant of interpolation quality. We represent textures as collections of local appearance vectors, or textons, and replace positional pairing with appearance-aware matching while keeping the encoder, representation, and decoder fixed. This isolates the effect of correspondence from changes in model capacity or training. Across texture pairs, appearance-aware matching consistently improves the distributional quality of interpolated midpoints over positional feature blending. Soft matching produces the strongest midpoint statistics, whereas one-to-one assignments yield more balanced transitions and closer agreement with the target endpoint. The same intervention also improves a second pretrained texture interpolator without retraining. These results identify correspondence as a first-class design choice in texture interpolation: meaningful transitions depend not only on how strongly two textures are mixed, but also on which local appearances are mixed with one another.

title: FastEEP: Fast Intra-Instance Elastic Scaling for Expert-Parallel MoE Serving
abstract: Large-scale expert parallelism (EP) has become the standard deployment configuration for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models in production. Meanwhile, the highly dynamic nature of LLM workloads requires providers to continuously adjust serving capacity to match fluctuating demand. Scaling MoE serving cannot be efficiently achieved by simply adding or removing serving instances; instead, it often requires resizing the EP group within an existing instance, which we refer to as intra-instance scaling.Existing inference engines primarily rely on instance-level scaling, which destroys and reconstructs entire serving instances, incurring substantial scaling overhead. We present FastEEP (Fast Elastic Expert Parallel), a fast intra-instance scaling system for MoE serving based on the principle of Partial Reuse. FastEEP reuses existing runtime state across worker execution, GPU memory, and communication by separating reusable execution structures from the resources activated by the current EP configuration. This separation enables coordinated resource reclamation and reconfiguration while preserving costly-to-reconstruct state, allowing fast EP scaling without full instance teardown and reconstruction. Our evaluation shows that FastEEP achieves 4.5x--11.7x faster scaling than the existing vLLM-based approach across different models, enabling efficient, fine-grained scaling of MoE serving.

title: Back to the Future: Reverse-Consequence Modeling for Long-Horizon Particle Dynamics
abstract: Accurate prediction of object trajectories is fundamental to mechanical understanding and robotic control. However, autoregressive models inherently suffer from cumulative errors, leading to severe drift in long-horizon rollouts. Observing that in many physical systems with dissipative or convergence-to-rest behavior, the final states are often more predictable than transient dynamics (e.g., a sliding object resting under friction or a pendulum stabilizing at equilibrium), we propose ReStep, a cascaded approach that reverses the conventional forward-prediction paradigm. ReStep first employs a stochastic model to directly predict the final state, then leverages Anchored Diffusion to generate goal-conditioned intermediate trajectories. By conditioning on both ''boundary states'', it effectively constrains dynamics and reduces uncertainty, producing physically plausible and temporally coherent transitions. We further integrate ReStep dynamics as the physical engine within a 3D Gaussian Splatting pipeline, enabling a unified physical-visual framework for intuitive inference from images. Extensive experiments on diverse rigid and non-rigid collision datasets show that ReStep achieves superior long-term accuracy, substantially mitigating error accumulation via reverse-consequence modeling.

title: Beyond Fixed Targets: On-Policy One-Shot Speaker Personalization for Autoregressive Text-To-Speech Models
abstract: One-shot personalization of autoregressive (AR) text-to-speech (TTS) models remains challenging because supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on a single reference pair rapidly degrades generation quality. We identify fixed, off-policy supervision as a key cause of failure in one-shot SFT for AR TTS, leading to blank or near-empty outputs at inference. Diversifying the training data with zero-shot pseudo-pairs eliminates this failure but yields little improvement in speaker similarity and increases word error rate because the targets remain fixed and teacher-forced. We therefore propose two on-policy approaches for one-shot speaker personalization: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with a speaker-similarity reward and On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) with soft supervision from a reference-conditioned teacher. Both on-policy methods improve speaker similarity while preserving intelligibility, with different trade-offs: GRPO achieves the strongest overall performance, whereas OPSD enables substantially faster adaptation without external reward evaluation. Further analysis confirms that these gains stem from on-policy supervision rather than target diversity, establishing on-policy training as an effective framework for one-shot AR TTS personalization.

title: Modular cryogenic link for microwave quantum communication over distances of tens of meters
abstract: Quantum technologies promise a radically new way to solve classically intractable computing problems. Superconducting circuits as a platform are at the forefront of this field. The cryogenic operation temperatures of superconducting circuits however impose challenges for the further scaling to many connected quantum information processing units into a local area or global network. In this work, we present a hardware solution for connecting quantum devices operating at microwave frequencies into local area networks, which enable the exchange of quantum information between spatially separated parties. Specifically, we demonstrate a modular system spanning distances of 5, 10 and 30 meters operated at cryogenic temperatures and connecting two superconducting circuit systems, located in individual dilution refrigerators, through a quantum communication channel. We develop a thermal model to evaluate the heat transfer processes in the setup, optimize the design and select appropriate materials for its construction. The assembled 30-meter-long system achieves operating temperatures of below 50 mK after a cooldown time of about six and a half days. This link enables the execution of distributed quantum computing and communication algorithms. It also adds the resource of non-locality, certified by a loophole-free Bell test, to the field of quantum science and technology with superconducting circuits.

title: Urine sediment classification using deep learning models
abstract: El análisis de sedimentos urinarios es una práctica fundamental en el diagnóstico clínico de patologías renales y urológicas. Sin embargo, su ejecución manual es dependiente del operador, consume tiempo y está sujeta a variabilidad subjetiva, mientras que los sistemas automatizados comerciales suelen resultar costosos para laboratorios de mediana escala. En este contexto, este trabajo aborda la aplicación de técnicas de aprendizaje profundo para la identificación y clasificación automática de partículas en imágenes microscópicas de sedimento urinario. Bajo una adaptación de la metodología CRISP-DM, se integran diversos conjuntos de datos multiclase mediante un proceso de estandarización de formatos compatibles con arquitecturas de detección de objetos como YOLO (You Only Look Once). El tratamiento de los datos prioriza la integridad de las muestras originales, evitando técnicas que pudieran alterar la distribución natural de las clases. El desbalance de clases se aborda mediante la configuración de las funciones de pérdida y las estrategias de aumento de datos aplicadas durante el entrenamiento. La evaluación del desempeño se realiza utilizando métricas como F1-Score, Sensibilidad y matrices de confusión, permitiendo un análisis detallado del comportamiento del modelo en distintas clases. Los resultados obtenidos evidencian un desempeño satisfactorio, lo que sugiere que el uso de modelos preentrenados junto con estrategias de ajuste fino constituye un enfoque prometedor para la automatización del análisis de sedimentos urinarios en contextos clínicos.

title: WP-647 — Exploring Mathematical Structures in Advanced AI Conversations
abstract: This paper investigates the mathematical constructs and structures evident in advanced artificial intelligence conversations, as evidenced by the analysis of a particular video presentation. By examining the frame-by-frame analysis and the mathematical frameworks discussed, we aim to establish connections between these frameworks and the broader implications for the E8 Intelligence model. The findings herein contribute to the understanding of the role of mathematical structures in enhancing AI communication and comprehension.

title: Reproducibility package: Which decisions will the next model change? A label-free budget and watchlist for AI model updates
abstract: Anonymous reproducibility package for a submission under double-blind review at Transactions on Machine Learning Research. Code for decision margins of typed rules (with an exact-margin oracle), budgets, finite-batch bounds and their coverage simulation, watchlists and pre-update baseline rankers, cross-version analyses; preregistrations of the two snapshots of the hosted model; result files and logs (state texts of public batteries hashed); the generator and the 300 synthetic invoices of the compliance demonstrator; the seeded builder of the multi-dataset battery with source hashes; the systematic review cited in the paper; and the LaTeX source with the script that redraws the figures. Code under MIT; data, logs and invoices under CC BY 4.0.

title: Artifact for Analyzing Unbounded Probabilistic Loops using Characteristic Function Recurrences
abstract: Artifact for the paper "Analyzing Unbounded Probabilistic Loops using Characteristic Function Recurrences", conditionally accepted at POPL 2027. The artifact is a VirtualBox virtual machine image (about 4.9 GB), downloadable as a .ova file (Artifact-VM.ova). It needs VirtualBox 7.1 or later. The guest is Ubuntu 24.04 LTS Desktop (x86-64), pre-configured with 8 GB RAM and 4 CPUs. No network access is needed inside the VM. The virtual machine was built and tested with VirtualBox 7.2.20 on Windows 11 Pro (x86-64), on an Intel Core Ultra 9 275HX laptop (24 cores, 32 GB RAM). We recommend that the artifact is run on hosts having at least 16 GB RAM. The artifact has not been tested on macOS, on Apple-silicon (ARM) hosts: since the image is x86-64 so we expect it to run slowly under emulation. For further information and instruction on how to run the artifact see README.md (also available in the VM at /home/artifact/Artifact/README.md).

title: Binary text classification using machine learning and transformer models for small and imbalanced datasets
abstract: Aims: The increasing speed with which platforms providing digital content have entered our lives has made the classification of the content on these platforms important. In this study, the binary classification problem of Netflix content as a movie or show was addressed, the effect of metadata features and text descriptions on an accurate classification process was examined and a new hybrid approach was presented. Methods: Two Netflix datasets from open sources (Kaggle and Hugging-Face) were used in the study. Furthermore, so as to eliminate the imbalance in the datasets, machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) models with Natural Language Processing (NLP) were used separately and hybridly on the two datasets downloaded for shows and movies, both individually and combined. In this way, the dataset was examined separately as imbalanced and balanced, and the imbalance was eliminated by merging two datasets. Results: The proposed hybrid framework achieved the results of 0,970940 accuracy, 0,982801 precision, 0,936768 recall and 0,959233 F1-score. Conclusion: It has been demonstrated through experimental results that the obtained results are better than those of other models. In the experiments, various machine learning methods and transformer based language models were evaluated; it was observed that the metadata-based models showed high performance in terms of accuracy, whereas BERT and similar models were particularly successful in detecting the ‘show’ class. The study reveals that the structured metadata and textual data are complementary in nature, and it is shown that hybrid approaches combining machine learning with transformer models would produce more balanced and robust results.

title: Beyond Time Induction: Structured Conditional Neural Solvers for Parametric Stochastic-Volatility Pricing
abstract: Physics-informed neural networks provide a flexible framework for learning parametric PDE solution families without labeled data, yet preserving accurate derivatives across heterogeneous regimes remains challenging. Structured neural solvers offer compact representations, but restrictive conditional parameterizations can limit adaptation across the solution family. We introduce BeTINN, a structured conditional architecture extending time-induced modulation through multi-directional time-parameter conditioning and a joint residual pathway. We evaluate BeTINN on the Heston stochastic-volatility PDE, a demanding parametric problem with mixed derivatives and economically relevant first- and second-order sensitivities. BeTINN improves joint accuracy across normalized option value and key sensitivity metrics relative to our baselines. Controlled ablations characterize the roles of its architectural components. We further find that validation physics loss is informative but does not fully determine differential fidelity, and that accurate solution values can coexist with localized derivative errors. These results support structured conditional adaptation and motivate derivative-aware evaluation when sensitivities are downstream quantities of interest.

title: Data Density Scaling Laws for Image Self-Distillation
abstract: Current scaling law formulations suggest that increasing the number of unique samples in a dataset improves model performance, while repeated exposure to the same samples provides diminishing value. In this work, we examine this assumption for image self-distillation models. Through systematic experiments across diverse datasets, namely Maxar, SATLAS, Waymo, nuPlan, Ego4D, ImageNet, and YFCC15M, we demonstrate that the effects of sample repetition on downstream performance are non-trivial and dataset-dependent. We identify settings where repeatedly training on a smaller random subset can outperform training on a larger set of unique samples. This finding highlights a limitation of existing scaling laws. To address this gap, we propose a modified version of a Chinchilla-style scaling law that explicitly accounts for two factors: the number of unique samples and repetition per sample. This formulation provides a framework for understanding data-compute trade-offs and improves prediction in some regimes where repetition plays a central role, although its benefits are not consistent across datasets. Finally, we examine how subset selection and augmentation affect downstream performance.

title: Autonomous Science Bench: Evaluating AI Agents for Autonomous Scientific Discovery
abstract: AI agents for autonomous scientific discovery must decide which experiments to run under a limited budget. Most benchmarks for science agents provide fixed datasets, while others that support active experimentation largely rely on simulation. We introduce Autonomous Science Bench, an initial release comprising six budgeted design-build-test-learn campaigns grounded in published experiments across biology, chemistry, and materials science. Agents select batches of designs, receive measurements from a lab service, and use the results to guide subsequent experiments before delivering a predictive model. Success requires passing two calibrated gates: a discovery gate, which evaluates the designs the agent measured, and a learning gate, which evaluates its model's ranking of held-out designs. In a pilot evaluation of eight agent-model configurations and 144 trials, the best configuration succeeds in 67% of trials, while the hardest campaign is solved in only three of 24 attempts. The two gates reveal different weaknesses: some agents build accurate rankings but find too few promising designs, while others find promising designs but fail to predict which unseen designs will perform well. These differences are obscured by overall success rates alone. We release version 0.1 of the campaigns, lab runtime, and public leaderboard at https://yibow.me/autonomous-science-bench.

title: CineMem: Attention-Aligned Fine-grained Memory Retrieval for Multi-Shot Long Video Generation
abstract: Autoregressive video generation relies on memory retrieval to model long-range dependencies. This capability becomes particularly critical for multi-shot generation, where models must reconcile substantial visual changes across shot transitions with persistent semantic continuity. Existing methods tend to perform memory retrieval at the frame level and share the same historical context across all query tokens, overlooking the heterogeneous information needs and leading to redundant retrieval and inefficient use of historical memory. To bridge this gap, we introduce CineMem, an attention-aligned fine-grained memory retrieval framework that combines online memory organization with query-adaptive retrieval for autoregressive multi-shot video generation. Specifically, guided by intrinsic memory-access patterns revealed through attention analysis, we propose an online-clustered KV cache as a memory organization strategy over all historical tokens, enabling semantic-aware memory grouping and more precise retrieval. In addition, we introduce a query-level retrieval mechanism that provides broader access to historical information under a fixed retrieval budget, thereby improving long-term memory utilization. Together, these designs enable the multi-shot video generator to preserve long-range consistency across shot transitions, particularly in revisitation scenarios, while approximating full-memory access under a constrained memory budget. To facilitate evaluation, we further introduce a suite of task-specific, VLM-assisted metrics for faithful inter-shot consistency assessment. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework.

title: From Token Correction to Claim Admission: Training-Free Hallucination Mitigation for Large Vision-Language Models
abstract: Large vision-language models often exhibit object hallucination, generating claims that are not supported by the input image. To mitigate this issue, we propose Evidence-Guided Visual Claim Admission (EGVCA), a training-free framework that admits a semantic claim only when it receives sufficient image-dependent support. EGVCA measures this support by comparing the claim likelihood under the observed image and a visual-null input. For captioning, it controls semantic expansion without altering token generation. For binary visual question answering, it combines atomic visual support with the image-induced change in the model's native Yes--No margin. Experiments on CHAIR, POPE, and MME across three LVLM backbones show that EGVCA substantially reduces object hallucination while preserving caption quality. It achieves the highest POPE F1 in eight of nine backbone--sampling settings and improves the native MME total score on all three backbones. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of claim-level admission as a simple alternative to token-level distribution correction.
